en: Four paths. Butcher said. Each takes a different road. That was the loyalty test. Choice was how loyalty showed. What you chose showed who you were.

speaker: narrator
en: Reza branch A. Revenge or forgiveness. Reza was still at the base. No longer prisoner status. Ambiguous after Butcher's decision. In the base but not a CV member.

speaker: butcher_vasquez
en: Reza caused harm to CV. Not small harm. The code doesn't forgive betrayal.

speaker: butcher_vasquez
en: But — you said that name. Aisha. That's why Reza is here. Your choice existed.

speaker: butcher_vasquez
en: Now you handle it. What to do.

speaker: narrator
en: Reza was there. In the corner. Hands unbound. But unable to leave. Unable to exit the CV base. Looked at you. Those eyes remembered. Aisha. Name.

speaker: reza
en: You said her name. To Butcher.

speaker: player
en: Aisha.

speaker: reza
en: That's why I'm here. Not dead.

speaker: reza
en: I'm not an informant. Really. But I have no way to prove it.

speaker: narrator
en: Couldn't tell if Reza's words were true. Evidence existed. Evidence in CV. But evidence could be manufactured. MCC might have made it. Unknown.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: Butcher left it to you. Just follow the code.

speaker: player
en: What's the code. In this situation.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: Betrayal isn't forgiven. That's the code. But your fifth code is different. Because you made it.

speaker: narrator
en: The fifth code. Each person makes their own. What Butcher had said. Didn't understand when first heard. Now understood. It was for this moment. For this choice.

speaker: player
en: Reza. One question.

speaker: reza
en: What.

speaker: player
en: Where is Aisha.

speaker: reza
en: Why.

speaker: player
en: A person with a name needs someone who knows that name.

speaker: narrator
en: Reza answered. Gave a location. Hellas Central. Small district. Name. Contact method. That was all Reza could give. Received it. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
en: Reported to Butcher. Result of the Reza branch. Butcher listened. No words. The prosthetic moved. That was all. That was acknowledgment.

speaker: narrator
en: Reza branch B. Extract intelligence. Reza knew things about MCC. Information CV needed. Crow knew that. But Reza hadn't spoken. There was a reason.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: Reza knows MCC C-zone movement routes. What we need.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: Won't talk. You try.

speaker: player
en: Why me.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: You said Aisha's name. That became trust. Maybe.

speaker: narrator
en: Went to Reza. Corner. Crow watching. But no words. When Crow was wordless it meant trust. Or waiting. Hard to distinguish.

speaker: player
en: Reza. MCC C-zone routes. You know them.

speaker: reza
en: Yes.

speaker: player
en: Tell me and you can leave here. I'll tell Butcher.

speaker: reza
en: Is that a lie?

speaker: player
en: No.

speaker: narrator
en: Reza thought. For a long time. Eyes closed. Hands unbound. Those hands on the knees. Not trembling. That was how this person was strong. The way of deciding.

speaker: reza
en: There's a west route in C-zone. MCC doesn't officially use it. But no guards. Empty passage. Old mine drainage.

speaker: reza
en: Rotation interval. Thirty minutes. Official guards are east. None west.

speaker: reza
en: That's all. Can I leave now?

speaker: narrator
en: Went to Butcher. Passed the information. Butcher listened. Crow confirmed. No words. But the look in their eyes changed. The information was correct. Could tell that.

speaker: butcher_vasquez
en: Release Reza.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: Butcher.

speaker: butcher_vasquez
en: It's the code. A promise was made. Keep it.

speaker: narrator
en: Reza left the base. Didn't look back. Walk wasn't fast. That was strange. Expected fast. But walked slowly. Steps of someone thinking.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher watched. Until Reza disappeared. That was all. That was Butcher's way. Watching. Watching for a long time. And saying nothing.

speaker: narrator
en: Marko branch. Negotiate with outside faction. Sandstone Junction. Middle of Mars. Neither MCC nor CV. Neutral ground. A meeting there. Marko Diel. Independent mercenary group leader.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: Marko has lived between MCC and CV. That's the advantage. Has information.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: You negotiate. I watch.

speaker: player
en: What are the conditions.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: That's the negotiation. You make them.

speaker: narrator
en: Marko arrived. Not alone. Two behind. Armed. That was the way in neutral ground. Meet armed. Trust without trust.

speaker: marko
en: Heard CV wants to negotiate. First time.

speaker: player
en: Not the first time.

speaker: marko
en: Butcher not coming in person is a first.

speaker: player
en: I came. That's enough.

speaker: narrator
en: Marko looked at you. For a long time. CV but a new face. A new face negotiating was strange. But that was Butcher's way. The way of testing new people.

speaker: marko
en: What are the conditions.

speaker: player
en: MCC D-zone intelligence. CV withdraws from Sandstone Junction. For one year.

speaker: marko
en: One year is long.

speaker: player
en: Better than short.

speaker: narrator
en: Marko thought. Crow watched from behind. Quiet. No words. Crow's way in negotiations was silence. Negotiation was reducing words. The person with fewer words won.

speaker: marko
en: Have D-zone intel. But not one year. Six months.

speaker: player
en: Eight months.

speaker: marko
en: Done.

speaker: narrator
en: Negotiation ended. Marko left. Crow approached. No expression. But spoke. Spoke for the first time. That was strange. Crow speaking after a negotiation.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: Eight months. Not bad.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: Butcher will be pleased. Won't show it, though.

speaker: narrator
en: Standard mission. Occupy mine district. Hellas outer mine. Abandoned by MCC. But things that could be used. Equipment. Passages. Things CV needed.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: Abandoned mine. But MCC comes intermittently. There's a reason.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: Something hidden there. We bring it back.

speaker: player
en: What's hidden.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: You'll know when we get there.

speaker: narrator
en: Into the mine. Dark. Light on. Passages. Old ones. Thirty years old. Before CV existed. Dug by miners. Now empty.

speaker: narrator
en: Something deeper in. Crates. MCC markings. But goods not in official records. Crow saw them. No expression. But the look changed. It was as expected.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: This is it. Weapon components. MCC was stockpiling them unofficially.

speaker: player
en: Why hide this here.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: Weapons not in official records have no official accountability. That's MCC's way.

speaker: narrator
en: Checked the crates. Weapon components. Large quantity. Things CV could use. Had to take them. But heavy. Hard to move fast.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: MCC is coming. Regular check. Twenty minutes.

speaker: player
en: How much can we take.

speaker: crow_reyes
en: Two crates. That's all. In twenty minutes.

speaker: butcher_vasquez
en: You kept the code.

speaker: butcher_vasquez
en: Few people in CV make their own code. Most don't even know what the code is. That's why they don't last.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher acknowledged. Words brief. That was his way. Fewer words meant more meaning. You kept the code. That meant you could be here, in this base.

speaker: narrator
en: The code was tested. Which code wasn't clear. On Mars the code was tested by situation. Situations taught it. Fire burned in barrels. The base was alive.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher spoke. Expel you or acknowledge you. Nothing in between. CV was that kind of place. No middle ground. But having no middle was actually clear. That was this base's way.

speaker: narrator
en: Fire burned. Night deepened. Cinder finished work. Something had been repaired. What it was she didn't say. Butcher sat by the fire. Looked down at the prosthetic. Made at seventeen. Thirty years old. Still working.

speaker: narrator
en: Good things were like that. Old but still working. The code was like that. Thirty years old. But still working. That was CV. The fire wasn't warm. But it burned.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder Grace was a person of few words. CV had many people of few words. But Cinder was different. Not that she couldn't speak. She didn't speak because she had too much to say.

speaker: narrator
en: She repaired machines. Things in the base. Broken things. Ruined things. Things no one else could fix. That was what Cinder did in CV. Repair. Not combat. Repair.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a time with MCC. Six years. A mechanical engineer. Tunnel support systems. Most important thing in Martian mines. When they collapsed people died. She was the person who prevented that. For six years.

speaker: narrator
en: Morning and Cinder came to you. First time. On her own. Usually Cinder didn't approach first. Touching the tool belt. That was her signal. Signal of something to say.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Can you come with me?

speaker: player
en: Where.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Hellas outer. Zone 12. Abandoned mine.

speaker: player
en: Any reason.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: I'll tell you when we get there.

speaker: narrator
en: Walked to the Hellas outskirts. The two of you. Cinder walked ahead. Not fast. But direction was clear. The walk of someone who knew this path. Had walked it before.

speaker: narrator
en: No words. Two hours walking. That wasn't strange. With Cinder silence was natural. Like the sound of tools. Present but natural as if absent.

speaker: narrator
en: Zone 12 visible. Abandoned mine. Entrance. Blocked. MCC marking. No entry. But an old marking. Three years old.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: This is it.

speaker: player
en: Where you worked before.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: For six years.

speaker: narrator
en: Into the mine. Dark. Cinder turned on a lamp. Passages. Old. Inside Cinder stopped. Looked at the wall. Put a hand on the wall. Didn't touch the tools. For the first time.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Eleven people died here.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Three years ago. Tunnel collapse. Not in MCC records. Erased.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder kept looking at the wall. Hand on the wall. Not moving. That was strange. Cinder's hands were always on tools. Hands that touched tools. Now on the wall. Cold wall.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: I was a mechanical engineer. In charge of tunnel support systems. For six years. If the systems were in order, people didn't die.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: I wrote a report. Support beam defects. Immediate repair required.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: The MCC supervisor returned it. Told me to revise. I didn't revise.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder walked along the passage. Inside. Deeper. Lamp lit the way. Walls closer. Passage narrowing. Then blocked. Stopped there. Couldn't tell where that was.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Here. Where the tunnel collapsed.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: One week after. One week after I submitted the report.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Eleven people were here. During a shift.

speaker: narrator
en: Wall blocked. Beyond it something. Where the eleven were. Couldn't reach there. Three years of that. Couldn't tell if Cinder had come here or not. But those footsteps looked like ones walked before.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: There are names. Eleven. Not in MCC records. But I have them. In this report.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Written three years ago. The original. What MCC couldn't take.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: I don't know why I'm telling you this. Just wanted to say it. For the first time.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder took out the report. From a pocket. Small. Folded. Many times. Taken out often. Folded often. The names were there. Eleven.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: MCC erased this from records. The accident became as if it never happened. The eleven became as if they never existed.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: I left MCC because of this. Not expelled. Left.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: That difference matters. To me.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder touched her tools. The ones on the belt. The ones that weren't weapons. That was her way. Touching tools settled thoughts. Three years of that. Not repairing tools but touching them. That was Cinder Grace's prayer.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: I didn't come to CV for money. I came because there was nowhere else to go.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Butcher heard about this. He came. Without a word. Just sat by the fire. Together. That was all. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher had lost an arm at seventeen. MCC had refused compensation. That and the eleven were the same thing. People whose names disappeared. People erased from records. People MCC deleted.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: I'm not only telling you.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Everyone on Mars should know. The names. People who died here. People not in the records.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: But I don't know how yet. How to tell them.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder folded the report again. Many times. Back into the pocket. Touched the tools again. Prayer ended. Thoughts settled.

speaker: narrator
en: Chose. Cinder looked. Those eyes were new. First time Cinder looked at you for a long time. Usually Cinder looked at tools. Machines. Walls. Didn't look at people long. But now looked.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: I'll read the names.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Can you listen?

speaker: player
en: Yes.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder took out the report again. Unfolded it. Names. Eleven. Read them. Slowly. One by one. Only names. No explanation. No explanation needed. There were names. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
en: Eleven names. Listened. Tried to remember. Didn't know if all eleven were possible. But listened. That was what Cinder wanted. Someone to listen.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder folded the report. Looking at the report there were tears. Not visible. Dark. But there was sound. Heard it. Pretended not to. That was the right thing.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Thank you.

speaker: player
en: For what.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: For listening. Just for listening.

speaker: narrator
en: Then sound. Outside. Toward the mine entrance. Footsteps. Multiple. MCC security. Not a regular check. Not supposed to come at this time. Something different.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: MCC. Why now.

speaker: player
en: Someone told them.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Because of the report. They know the report exists. Have always known.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder gripped the report. Back into the pocket. Touched the tools. That was a signal. Signal of preparation. Not preparing to fight. Something else. Preparing to flee. Or to protect.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Need to leave. There's another exit. Worked here three years. I know.

speaker: player
en: The report.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Taking it. It's in memory too. But paper lasts longer.

speaker: narrator
en: Out of the abandoned mine. Cinder came out with the report. What she'd carried for three years. The names were there. Eleven. On Mars a person with a name remained there. Even without a record. Even when abandoned.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: We're out.

speaker: player
en: The report too.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Yes. That too.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder touched the tool belt. Habit. Everything was there. Nothing missing. The eleven were gone. But the tools were there. The report was there. The memory was there.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC security came. Abandoned but there were guards. MCC guarded even abandoned mines. Things to erase there. No report. But it was in Cinder's memory. Memory had no security.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Lost the report.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: But the names are here.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: In memory. You heard them too. That's enough.

speaker: narrator
en: Back to base. Butcher was there. Before the fire. Cinder reported. Briefly. Butcher listened. No words. Looked down at the prosthetic. That was all.

speaker: butcher_vasquez
en: I know the names.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: You knew?

speaker: butcher_vasquez
en: From the beginning. Knew why Cinder came to CV. That's why you're here.

speaker: narrator
en: The sun tilted toward Erebus. Martian sun. Small thing. Distant thing. Cinder checked the tool belt again. Habit. Everything was there. Nothing missing. The eleven were gone. But the tools were there. The report was there. The memory was there. Fire burned. Not warm. But burning.

speaker: narrator
en: The outer edge of Kepler Crater. FSP was inside. The day Liang Wei declared. CV watched from outside. That was CV's position. Not inside. That had always been CV's position.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher came. That was rare. Butcher leaving the base. Left arm prosthetic. Old mining type. He had a coat. His hand was in the pocket. What was in that pocket was known. A photo. Thirty years old.

speaker: butcher
en: Kepler belongs to nobody?

speaker: butcher
en: Thirty years ago there were those words too. That the mines didn't belong to anyone. That they belonged to the miners. You know what happened after that.

speaker: butcher
en: Watch anyway. Cinder said this time might be different.

speaker: narrator
en: A sound came from inside the crater. Liang Wei's voice. The declaration. The voice of someone who had waited alone for thirty years. Butcher listened. The hand in the coat pocket didn't move. That was how Butcher paid attention. Didn't take out the photo. Listened.

speaker: cinder
en: Lena from FSP side is visible.

speaker: cinder
en: The person I saw at Sandstone. The fast one. With names on her arm.

speaker: cinder
en: We can protect Kepler together. The Sandstone Promise gets its meaning here.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC drones were in the sky above. One. Then two. Three. While the declaration proceeded inside the crater the drones multiplied. MCC was waiting. For when to intervene. Butcher looked at the sky. He took his hand from the coat pocket. Didn't take out the photo. Just the hand.

speaker: narrator
en: The CV scouting team had come here two days ago. From outer Hellas to Kepler. Red plains. Central Mars. Monotonous terrain. But monotonous terrain was easy to hide in. Twelve came. Without sound.

speaker: cinder
en: Half a day to cross the plains. Avoiding drones.

speaker: cinder
en: I know why Butcher came himself. There was something here thirty years ago.

speaker: butcher
en: Too many words.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher walked first. The scouting team followed. The plains were wide. Wind blew low. Dust flew at ankle height. Kepler Crater was on the horizon. Still small. But Butcher's steps were fast. This person knew this direction.

speaker: narrator
en: They passed the exterior of Erebus Crater. CV territory boundary. From here it was neutral ground. Land nobody owned. That was the character of central Mars. Lands not yet worth owning. Until the Ancient Metal discovery.

speaker: cinder
en: Past Erebus the MCC drone density changes. Equipment check here.

speaker: butcher
en: Fine.

speaker: cinder
en: Butcher. Bad day. Your face says so.

speaker: butcher
en: Wherever you need to go, you go regardless of the day.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher's health was deteriorating. Inside CV it was known. Lungs. Old mine dust. Different from Martian dust. Earth mine dust. Things from thirty years ago remained inside the body. Doing their work slowly.

speaker: narrator
en: They arrived at Kepler. The sun was tilting. Crater edge. Dust lay low. Couldn't see inside. Only sound. People gathered. Many people. More than expected.

speaker: cinder
en: Those are all miners.

speaker: cinder
en: Not just FSP. From Hellas villages too. Word spread.

speaker: butcher
en: What is this.

speaker: narrator
en: People were at the crater edge. Miners. Tool belts. Helmets. Nameless people. Those who lived nameless on Mars had gathered. Come to hear Liang Wei's declaration. They were silent. Waiting.

speaker: cinder
en: Look at those people.

speaker: cinder
en: Some are CV people. Miners from our territory side.

speaker: cinder
en: Don't know if that can be called a faction.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder was watching people. Judging. This person tested. Always. By situation. By people's reactions. Right now these people were being tested. By coming and waiting they were already saying something.

speaker: narrator
en: Then it was heard. Liang Wei's voice. From inside the crater. Without amplification. Bare voice. But it was heard. The shape of the crater held sound. Everyone heard it.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Below Kepler Crater there is Ancient Metal. It belongs to Mars. Not to any company. Not to any faction. This metal belongs to everyone.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Thirty years of data. This must become Article 1 of the draft Mars Constitution.

speaker: narrator
en: Silence. Then sound. The sound of miners. Not applause. Not words. The sound of helmets being struck. Mine signal. Agreement. That was their way. Learned in the noise of machines.

speaker: cinder
en: That is a weapon.

speaker: butcher
en: What?

speaker: cinder
en: She said draft constitution. It doesn't exist yet. But she said it. Some things come into being the moment they're spoken.

speaker: cinder
en: Those people just became witnesses to it.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher listened. For a long time. The hand in the coat pocket moved. Touching the photo. Didn't take it out. Just touched. There had been a declaration thirty years ago. Back then it was different. No miners. No witnesses.

speaker: butcher
en: Thirty years ago I heard it too. Similar words.

speaker: butcher
en: Back then there weren't people like those. Not that many.

speaker: cinder
en: That's why this time is different.

speaker: narrator
en: An MCC drone descended. One of them. From observation altitude to approach altitude. That was a signal. MCC was going to intervene. The miners saw it. The drone. The sound diminished. The helmet-striking stopped. But nobody moved.

speaker: cinder
en: Drone coming down. Two minutes to approach range.

speaker: cinder
en: We can take two of three with our equipment.

speaker: butcher
en: Then MCC sees this as war.

speaker: cinder
en: It already is war.

speaker: narrator
en: It was also possible to sell to MCC. This information. Liang Wei's location. The content of the data. CV was neutral. Still. That could have a price. Cinder seemed to know that thought. She touched her tools. Checking.

speaker: cinder
en: Don't think about selling to MCC.

speaker: cinder
en: There was a promise at Sandstone. I remember that promise.

speaker: cinder
en: Look at those people. Can you sell those people out?

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher looked. At the miners. Those who had struck their helmets. Nameless people. Different from the people in the thirty-year-old photo. Different but the same. Things at the same place for the same reason. He took out the photo. For the first time.

speaker: butcher
en: These people.

speaker: butcher
en: Photo from thirty years ago. Similar. Different faces though.

speaker: cinder
en: Butcher took out the photo.

speaker: butcher
en: You saw? Now decide.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a decision. Cinder reacted. She moved her tools. Butcher looked at the photo. For a long time. Then put it back in the pocket. Putting it back was different from taking it out. Thirty years ago there had been no reason to take it out. Today there was.

speaker: butcher
en: Today we did what couldn't be done thirty years ago.

speaker: butcher
en: Someone made a declaration back then too. Back then nobody protected it.

speaker: cinder
en: Now we protected it.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC sealed the crater. Butcher watched. His hand went back in the coat pocket. Rested on the photo. Same as thirty years ago. The difference was that Cinder was beside him.

speaker: narrator
en: The battle ended. The drones retreated. Or were gone. That was today's outcome. The miners were still there. Nameless people. Standing holding helmets. Facing Kepler Crater.

speaker: cinder
en: FSP looked weak. At first.

speaker: cinder
en: But those people came. Not called. FSP didn't call them. Those people came on their own.

speaker: cinder
en: That is FSP's strength. First time I understood that.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher took out the photo. Again. Second time. Twice in thirty years. Today. Looked at the miners. Looked at the photo. Looked at the miners again. The people in the photo and the people outside. Different. But the same.

speaker: butcher
en: Cinder.

speaker: cinder
en: Yes.

speaker: butcher
en: The Sandstone Promise. That was here today.

speaker: cinder
en: I know. I said I remember promises.

speaker: narrator
en: The sun had completely tilted. Kepler was red. People began to scatter. Miners. Each in their own direction. Didn't stay long. Came. Watched. Left. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder looked at Kepler. The crater. Deep and dark. Ancient Metal inside. Extraterrestrial origin. Belonging to Mars. That was now declared. A declaration couldn't be undone. Whatever MCC might do.

speaker: cinder
en: Boss. Do you know what we did today?

speaker: cinder
en: We took a side. CV taking sides is rare.

speaker: cinder
en: But this is right. First time I'm certain of that today.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher heard it. Cinder's words. No reaction. That was the reaction. This person did nothing when he agreed. Doing nothing was agreement. An old way. Learned in the mines.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC was still far. The drones had retreated. But hadn't disappeared. They would come tomorrow. More of them. That was known. But today CV was at the edge of Kepler. The Sandstone Promise had been here.

speaker: narrator
en:
Kepler turned red. Butcher took his hand from the coat pocket. Not the photo. Just the hand. Cinder watched that hand. The hand that didn't meet the prosthetic. The right hand. The people in the thirty-year-old photo would still be there. Only in the photo. But today they were also here at the edge of Kepler. Because of the declaration.

Cinder saw FSP differently for the first time. That was what happened today. That was what the Sandstone Promise had done.

speaker: narrator
en: The deepest part of the Erebus base. Called the throne hall. Butcher liked that name. There was no throne. There was one chair. An old one. A mining chair. Taken from an MCC mine. Thirty years ago. That was the throne.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher was sitting there. Holding the photo. First time seeing it. Outside the pocket. Black and white. Old. Thirty years. There were people. Several. Miners. One of them looked like Butcher. Young. Seemed about seventeen.

speaker: butcher
en: Sit.

speaker: butcher
en: Thirty years ago. The people in this photo. MCC mine. It was Hellas Zone 4. There was a strike.

speaker: butcher
en: MCC ended it. The strike. How, you already know without me saying. I survived. Among the people in this photo I'm the only one who lived.

speaker: narrator
en: The left arm. Prosthetic. Old mining type. Made by himself when MCC refused injury compensation. At seventeen. Thirty years since then. The same hand that made the prosthetic was now holding the photo. The right hand. Not trembling. No one had ever seen this man's hand tremble.

speaker: butcher
en: Zone 12. I was there. The night before the accident. Someone called me. Outside the base. Didn't say why. I went.

speaker: butcher
en: When I came back the next morning there was no tunnel. No people. Just dirt.

speaker: butcher
en: For thirty years I've thought about one thing. Why was I called.

speaker: narrator
en: Flashback. The tunnel. Thirty years ago. Dark. Two hundred meters underground on Mars. Ore dust. Narrow passage. Several people working. Sounds were heard. Metal sounds. Ground sounds. That was the sound of a living tunnel. Miners knew that sound.

speaker: narrator

en: Inside the mine. Dark. Only some lights alive. Tunnels. Narrow ones. From their end a sound came. Voices. Voices of living people.

speaker: narrator
en: Forty-nine were alive. Six injured. Two critically. Lena went in first. Looking for Park Sung-jin. Found. That name. The name on the arm. That living name.

speaker: lena
en: Alive. Forty-nine. Six injured. Two critical. Extraction complete.

speaker: lena
en: Sung-jin too. Alive.

speaker: mikhail
en: Good work. Truly.

speaker: mikhail
en: The miners are still inside. MCC tightened the seal. We need to rethink.

speaker: lena
en: Boss, next time we do it differently. Sung-jin is still inside. Still.

speaker: narrator
en: Miners came out. One by one. They received light. The morning light of Mars. It touched them. Someone shielding their eyes. Someone just standing. One person knelt. Touched the ground. The Martian earth. The red thing.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena was with Park Sung-jin. No words. Two people. The name on the arm. The living name. That was here now.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC lifted the seal. There was a formal protest. That was for later. What mattered now was that forty-nine were outside. Tea was waiting. Mikhail's tea.

speaker: narrator
en:
The tea had gone cold. Mikhail looked at the two cups. One was empty. The other was untouched. The person hadn't drunk it. Had held it and set it down.

Mikhail didn't find this strange. People who came to Mars came in their own ways. What mattered was that the cup had been accepted. With both hands.

And forty-nine were outside. That mattered too.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena Torres was a fast person. Fast walk, fast talk, fast judgment. A tattoo on her left arm. Names. Family names. Wrist to shoulder. When she moved fast those names moved with her.

speaker: narrator
en: When those names had come to be wasn't known. They must have come one by one. A name being added wasn't someone being born. It was someone disappearing. That was why they became tattoos. Engraving lost things on the body.

speaker: narrator
en: A miner had died. Mine 7 on the outer Hellas belt. Tunnel collapse. MCC territory. MCC sealed the accident. No notice to the family. No notice was the notice. On Mars that kind of notice came often.

speaker: narrator
en: The name was Park Sung-jin. Thirty-four. Two daughters. From Hellas mining village. Three years on the rotation at Mine 7. Three days ago the body was found. MCC didn't extract it. Said accident investigation in progress. Three days had passed.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. You're here.

speaker: lena
en: MCC blocked the area. Couldn't recover the body. Family's been waiting outside. Three days now.

speaker: lena
en: His name is Park Sung-jin. Thirty-four. Two daughters. Older one is seven. Younger is four.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena's left arm was visible. The tattoo. The names. How many of those names had come this way was not something to ask. She hadn't said. Fast people often had things they didn't say.

speaker: narrator
en: The family was there. Outside the perimeter. A woman with two children. The older child held the younger one's hand. The woman stood. Did nothing. Only waited. On Mars waiting was work.

speaker: lena
en: MCC perimeter. Two signs. Two guards. One drone behind.

speaker: lena
en: They say no entry until investigation complete. They won't say when that will be.

speaker: narrator
en: There was an MCC perimeter line. Signs. Two guards. Inside the tunnel was a body. The family waited. Sand rode the wind. Mars was not kind to those who waited.

speaker: narrator
en: One of the guards moved. Walked toward the family. Said something. The woman didn't respond. The guard returned. The small child cried. The older one comforted. A seven-year-old comforting a four-year-old.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. Heard what that guard said.

speaker: lena
en: Told them to go home. Come back tomorrow. Said they'd contact when the body comes out. Said if there's no contact there's no contact.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena's arm was visible. Her fist was clenched. The tattoo names bunched together. That was how Lena held back anger. Clenching a fist. Clenching names inside it. The names holding her.

speaker: narrator
en: Action was taken. MCC responded. Whether it was negotiation or confrontation or documentation. Something moved. On Mars what moved was what was alive.

speaker: lena
en: Done. The family took him.

speaker: lena
en: The older daughter said thank you. The seven-year-old. In Mars language.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. You did well today. Really.

speaker: lena
en: Couldn't get him out. The family is still outside.

speaker: lena
en: We try again. We remember Park Sung-jin. The name is on the arm.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC didn't issue a formal apology. No compensation. No accident report came out. That was for later. For now the family had taken the body. That was today's thing.

speaker: narrator
en: Two children went. The woman went. Didn't look back. The mine was there. Mine 7. MCC perimeter still there. Signs. Guards. Drone. And inside there was nothing. Now.

speaker: mikhail
en: Heard the report.

speaker: mikhail
en: MCC was probably trying to hide the accident details. Likely a tunnel support problem. They delayed the repair because of cost.

speaker: mikhail
en: Sung-jin was thirty-four. Seventeen years in the mines. He entered the mines before I made FSP.

speaker: narrator
en: Mikhail made tea. The right hand supported the left. The same way. Always the same way. Even after hearing accident news. Even after hearing news of death. That way didn't change. Having something that didn't change was important.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena came. Looked at her arm. The names. Didn't write a new name. Not yet. That was for later. For now she was holding it. That too was a way.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. This is the first.

speaker: lena
en: A miner dead on Mars. Family waiting. MCC blocking. This will keep happening. Today is not the last.

speaker: lena
en: But today it worked. The family took Sung-jin.

speaker: narrator
en: Night. FSP base. A few lights. People. People who knew today's news. But they didn't speak. Not speaking was respect. On Mars silence was sometimes like that.

speaker: narrator
en: There was evidence. Site documentation. Some MCC supervisor communication records. Support repair requests had been made three times. Three times refused. Because of cost. That was in the record.

speaker: mikhail
en: We have this record. Three refusals. That's MCC's negligence.

speaker: mikhail
en: But to become evidence it needs official channels. FSP can submit it. Through the assembly.

speaker: mikhail
en: It takes time. MCC will block it. But it has to be done.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena looked at her arm. In the dark. The tattoo was visible. The names. One by one. Under some names there was a date. The day they disappeared. The day of disappearing was engraved.

speaker: narrator
en: The next day Mine 7 was seen again. Perimeter. Signs. Guards. But different. One of the MCC guards watched. Eyes met. That person looked away first. That was saying something.

speaker: narrator
en: Mine 7 was there. Nothing inside. Still a sign saying investigation in progress. When that would come down wasn't known. But there was a record. Three refusals. That wouldn't come down.

speaker: narrator
en:
Mikhail made tea. Two cups. Poured with both hands. Lena came in. She drank hers. This time the other person drank too. One miner was dead. That didn't change. But the tea was warm.

There was evidence. Three refusals. That didn't change either. There were two kinds of things that didn't change. Death and records. Both were here today.

speaker: narrator
en: A village. Outside the MCC mine. Not an official settlement. A temporary residential zone. On Mars temporary meant lasting. A twenty-year temporary village. People were born there and worked there. Some died there.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC issued an order. Zone evacuation. Two weeks. No reason given. Orders without reason were the most frightening thing on Mars. If there was a reason there was room to argue. Without a reason there was nowhere to argue.

speaker: narrator
en: The village had a cemetery. Miners' graves. Names were there. Some written in chalk. Some engraved on metal plates. Old. New. Mixed. What to do with that cemetery was also not in the order.

speaker: mikhail
en: There are sixty people here.

speaker: mikhail
en: Half are leaving. Half say they'll stay. People who know what happens if they stay and still say they'll stay.

speaker: mikhail
en: Yuna is trying to convince the villagers. She's twenty-one. Born here.

speaker: narrator
en: Yuna Kim. Born on Mars. Raised in this village. Her father was in the cemetery. That name was there. On a metal plate. An old one. But polished like new.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a fire. Outside fire was dangerous on Mars. But these people had one. They must have for twenty years. Mikhail made tea. The right hand supported the left. It was the same here. Lena held her left arm in the firelight. The tattoo was visible. The names swayed.

speaker: yuna
en: Boss. If sixty people stay MCC can't force removal. There's a Mars residency clause.

speaker: yuna
en: Right now there are thirty. We need thirty more. The neighboring village can come. If FSP supports it.

speaker: yuna
en: There's a cemetery here too. My father is there too. There's a name.

speaker: narrator
en: The fire burned. Mikhail's tea cooled. He drank it. Holding the cup with both hands. This man had been a miner. Before he made FSP. First generation on Mars. That was in those two hands. The hands of this village's people were the same. Same dust. Same calluses.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a neighboring village. Hellas outer Zone C. Twenty people lived there. Also MCC territory. Also had an evacuation order. If the two villages combined that was fifty. Ten short for the residency clause. There was another place. Farther away.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. Yuna is right. Sixty is the number. Legally.

speaker: lena
en: But there's a problem. If the neighboring village people come MCC seals that village too. Both villages get tied together.

speaker: lena
en: Don't know if that's good or bad.

speaker: narrator
en: Yuna looked toward the cemetery. In the dark. Metal plates glinted in the firelight. Names. Those seemed to be listening to this discussion now. Protecting where names were and protecting people who had names. Whether those were the same thing or different.

speaker: yuna
en: Father died here. Mining accident. When I was eight. Mother said she couldn't leave. Because father's name is here.

speaker: yuna
en: I feel the same. But the living matter more. Father would have thought so too.

speaker: narrator
en: The fire burned. The village was quiet. People were gathered. Each with their own thoughts. The weight of staying. The weight of leaving. On Mars when choosing between two things both were heavy. Sometimes there was no good choice.

speaker: narrator
en: There was an MCC order. Two weeks. No reason. It was over this village. Over the names. Over the children. Over the fire. There was a way to make it void. Sixty people. Residency rights. But that might not be a resolution.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a decision. It became movement. People moved. On Mars people moving meant something was decided. Without a decision there was no movement. With a decision movement was fast.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC came. Of course. When there was movement MCC came. Guards. Drones. Official documents. That was MCC's way. Coming officially. That was the most frightening thing.

speaker: yuna
en: We have the right to be here. The residency clause.

speaker: yuna
en: There are sixty people here. Count them. Sixty.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC counted. Actually. One by one. That was how the bureaucratic thing worked. Count. Record. Count again. Yuna waited. Didn't move. Sixty people didn't move.

speaker: yuna
en: They stayed. Sixty stayed.

speaker: yuna
en: MCC left. Officially they're reviewing the documents.

speaker: mikhail
en: I went to Yuna's father's grave this morning. There was a name. Not erased.

speaker: narrator
en: The village emptied. The fire went out. The cemetery remained. The names remained. What MCC would do with a cemetery that had names was unknown. It was not a thing to want to know.

speaker: narrator
en: Dawn broke. Light came to the village. Sixty people. Children came out. Those children ran through the village. Adults watched. Some smiled. Some just watched. Both were right.

speaker: narrator
en: Light reached the cemetery. Names received the light. Metal plates. Chalk names. Old. New. Mixed. The light touched them evenly. That was what Martian morning light was like. It didn't distinguish.

speaker: yuna
en: Boss. Thank you.

speaker: yuna
en: Father is here. Maybe that's not what matters. But it matters to me.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena stood before the cemetery. Looked at her left arm. The names on the arm. Whether any of them were among those here couldn't be known. Mars was wide. Names were scattered. But what was engraved was engraved.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC documents were still being processed. That would take a long time. MCC documents always took a long time. That too was a method. Pressuring with time. But right now there were sixty people. As long as sixty were here the documents had to wait.

speaker: narrator
en: Yuna bowed toward the cemetery. That was all. No words. That was her way. There was quiet courage. Courage that didn't speak loudly. That was how she had led sixty people.

speaker: narrator
en:
Dawn broke. Mikhail made new tea. Several cups. The right supported the left. Yuna received tea. With both hands. That was learned. Learned tonight. Learned in this village. The tea was warm.

Sixty stayed. The cemetery stayed. The names stayed. The temporary village on Mars. Twenty years old. Surviving one more day.

speaker: narrator
en: Sandstone Junction. Central Mars. Not in any faction's territory. Which was why all three factions passed through it. The sand was red. Old footprints on the sand. All came from different directions. All left in different directions.

speaker: narrator
en: Sandstone. Sand and stone. The name had a reason. Here the road split in three. Hellas. Erebus. Olympus. Three directions. Somewhere between them MCC existed. Not visible but present.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder Grace had arrived first. CV. Tool belt. Oil on her hands. This was someone who worked everywhere. Even when there was no work she looked like she was working. That was her way.

speaker: narrator
en: The tool belt told you. Worn things. Much used. Not used carelessly. Used precisely. Tools spoke of who used them. This person was a repairer. Not a destroyer. Those two were different.

speaker: cinder
en: FSP came.

speaker: cinder
en: Butcher didn't want this meeting. I convinced him. It took a long time.

speaker: cinder
en: Once only. If a promise is made here today it is a promise. CV remembers promises. Learned that in the mines.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder ran her hand over the tool belt. Unconscious. This was her check. Whether everything was there. Nothing missing. She was a person who confirmed what was present. Not a person who searched for what was lost.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. Can I speak?

speaker: lena
en: Cinder. FSP trusts CV. Do you know what that means? There aren't many things we trust.

speaker: lena
en: There are names on my arm. Among them are CV people too.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder looked at Lena's arm. Looked for a long time. Didn't touch her tools. That was this person's attention. When she didn't touch her tools she was thinking something. Perhaps she was reading the names.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder's eyes stopped at a certain name. Recognizing. What that was couldn't be known. But there was a stopping. Names did that. A known name stopped the eyes.

speaker: cinder
en: That's a Zone 12 name.

speaker: lena
en: Yes.

speaker: cinder
en: Three years ago. I was there.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena looked down at her arm. That name. Zone 12. A name two people knew. One had engraved it on their arm. One had been there three years ago. That was at Sandstone now.

speaker: cinder
en: I'll state the terms of the promise. FSP recognizes CV territory. CV doesn't touch FSP workers. If MCC attacks we hold together.

speaker: cinder
en: That's all. Simple. Simple things last.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena listened. It was a moment when a fast person became slow. A promise. Zone 12 name. Tool belt. Those things were at this junction. Sandstone. A place with a name for a reason.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC wasn't visible. But that didn't mean absent. A drone was probably somewhere. Observing. MCC was always observing. That made this promise more important. Promises made before those who watched had different weight.

speaker: cinder
en: MCC is watching. There's a drone to the east.

speaker: cinder
en: That's fine. A promise can be made where it's seen. Sturdier than promises made where they can't be seen.

speaker: narrator
en: The sun tilted. The sand of Sandstone turned redder. Three directions. Hellas. Erebus. Olympus. Between them two people stood. FSP. CV. And one name. Zone 12.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder said nothing. She took something from the tool belt. A small metal pin. She pushed it into the ground. Into the sand. What it was couldn't be known. No explanation. She just did it. This was Cinder's way. Testing with something other than words.

speaker: cinder
en: Do you know what this is?

speaker: lena
en: Mine boundary pin. CV marker.

speaker: cinder
en: If I plant it here it means CV territory.

speaker: cinder
en: I won't plant it. Not today.

speaker: narrator
en: That was the test. Not planting the pin. Leaving Sandstone as belonging to neither side. That was the first condition for this promise to be possible. Cinder didn't say it in words. She did it with action. The action of not planting the pin.

speaker: cinder
en: Second.

speaker: cinder
en: If I turn my back what will you do.

speaker: lena
en: Wait.

speaker: cinder
en: Good.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder turned her back. Looked in one direction. Toward Erebus. Something was there. Or wasn't. Unknowable. But Cinder looked that way. For a long time. That was the second test. Showing her back.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder turned around again. She took something from the tool belt. A small knife. Flat. For mining. She drew it across her left palm. Slowly. Without sound. Blood came.

speaker: cinder
en: This is how contracts are made on Mars.

speaker: cinder
en: Cut each other's hands and shake. That is the contract.

speaker: cinder
en: This is a contract. On Mars a contract is valid even in death.

speaker: narrator
en: The knife came across. From Cinder's hand. To this side. Lena looked. Cinder's bleeding hand. It was waiting. A hand bleeding alone. Waiting for an answer.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. Do I need to do it too?

speaker: cinder
en: Someone with decision-making authority in FSP needs to do it.

speaker: lena
en: Boss does it. Boss is FSP here.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a decision. Cinder heard. There was a reaction. She touched her tools. Or she didn't. What came next differed by that. At Sandstone decisions were like that. Small things made large things.

speaker: narrator
en: Blood mixed. Or didn't. That was today's business at Sandstone. There was a handshake. Or there wasn't. But that two people had stood at this junction didn't change. The arm with the Zone 12 name. The tool belt with the mine knife.

speaker: cinder
en: MCC drone has been watching. Since before.

speaker: lena
en: MCC recorded this.

speaker: cinder
en: Good. If it's recorded it can't be undone.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder wrapped her hand. With cloth. Taken from the tool belt. Something she had prepared. This person had come knowing this. The bleeding. The wrapping. Things prepared. That was this person's way. Planning and acting.

speaker: narrator
en: Dust rose from the Erebus direction. Not wind. Movement. CV people were there. Things that had been waiting. Waiting for Cinder's signal. Not coming this way now. Waiting. That was what Cinder had done. Came alone but not alone.

speaker: lena
en: There are people on the Erebus side.

speaker: cinder
en: Our people. Butcher sent them.

speaker: lena
en: You said Butcher didn't want this meeting.

speaker: cinder
en: Even not wanting it, he prepared. That is Butcher.

speaker: cinder
en: It's a promise.

speaker: cinder
en: CV remembers promises. Said we learned it in the mines. In the mines one promise saves a life.

speaker: cinder
en: The Zone 12 name. The one on the arm. I remember.

speaker: narrator
en: No promise. Only footprints remained at the junction. Each in their own direction. Which direction Cinder went was not seen. Sandstone remained as it was. A place with a name for a reason. Sand and stone. Good for promises. Good for keeping them too. But not today.

speaker: narrator
en: The MCC drone moved away. It had seen. It had recorded. That was MCC's way. Seeing. Recording. Then deciding. What it was deciding now couldn't be known.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena looked at her arm. Zone 12 name. Cinder had known that name. She had been there. That was what had happened here today. Together with a promise. Or without one.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder looked at her wrapped hand. The cloth. Something she had prepared. This person had come today knowing this would happen. That the promise would be this way. Or not this way. Prepared for both. That was CV's way.

speaker: cinder
en: There's business at Kepler Crater. Liang Wei will make a declaration.

speaker: lena
en: You knew that too?

speaker: cinder
en: That's why today here mattered. Before Kepler.

speaker: narrator
en: The Sandstone Promise was before Kepler. There was an order. First the promise. Then Kepler. That was Cinder's plan. This person planned and acted. Not just acted. That was the difference from Butcher.

speaker: lena
en: What happened at Zone 12.

speaker: cinder
en: Won't say.

speaker: lena
en: That's fine. It's already on the arm. It's mine.

speaker: cinder
en: Yes. It's yours.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder looked toward Erebus. She signaled. With her hand. The CV people that way moved. Moving away. That was it for today. Business at the junction had ended. Or begun.

speaker: narrator
en:
Alone at the junction. The sun tilted. The sand turned red. Footprints scattered in three directions. There had been a meeting on Mars. There had been a promise. That promise would change the future of Mars. Or it would be erased by wind like the sand of Sandstone. Which it would be was not yet known.

But the Zone 12 name was on two arms. One as a tattoo. One as memory. That the wind couldn't erase.

speaker: narrator
en: Kepler Crater. Three kilometers deep. Where Liang Wei had surveyed alone for thirty years. Nobody had supported her. Not MCC. Not FSP. She came alone. Stayed alone for thirty years. She was the oldest thing in this crater.

speaker: narrator
en: Liang Wei Jin. Geologist. First generation Mars settler. Seventies. People in their seventies on Mars were rare. Most had left. To Earth. Or farther. Liang Wei had stayed. Because of Kepler.

speaker: narrator
en: Ancient Metal. The extraterrestrial origin hypothesis. MCC knew. MCC intended to monopolize it. Before that Liang Wei had contacted FSP. She didn't explain why. But the reason was visible. Someone who had been alone for thirty years wanted to share something. Especially something important.

speaker: narrator
en: The crater floor. Light came in. Morning light. The angle was special. Only at this time did the angle become this. Liang Wei knew. Thirty years had made it known. The light touched something. Something like metal. But not metal.

speaker: liang_wei
en: You came. FSP.

speaker: liang_wei
en: I first saw this thirty years ago. Couldn't tell anyone. Felt like it would disappear if I did. There are discoveries like that. Things that get taken away the moment you speak them.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Now I'll say it. Below Kepler Crater there is Ancient Metal. It belongs to Mars. Not to MCC. Not to FSP. Not to CV.

speaker: narrator
en: Words were spoken. What had not been said for thirty years was said now. The air changed. The air inside the crater. Thin. Cold. But those words were there. Harder than metal.

speaker: lena
en: Thirty years.

speaker: lena
en: You were here alone for thirty years?

speaker: liang_wei
en: Not alone. This was here. And there was data. With data you're not alone.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena's left arm was visible. Tattoo. Names. Whether any of those names were connected to this crater was unknown. But the way Lena listened to this declaration was different. It was a moment when a fast person became slow.

speaker: liang_wei
en: There is data. Thirty years of it. Analysis. Extraterrestrial origin hypothesis papers. Three of them. Unpublished.

speaker: liang_wei
en: MCC knew. My communications were monitored. For two years. That's why contacting FSP was also delayed.

speaker: narrator
en: An MCC drone was visible above the crater. One. For observation. MCC was always observing. That was MCC's way on this planet. Sometimes it couldn't be seen. But that didn't mean it wasn't there.

speaker: narrator
en: The drone became two. Then three. Observation intensified. That meant MCC had learned something. Liang Wei's declaration had already reached MCC. Or the drones had been listening here.

speaker: liang_wei
en: I see the drones. MCC.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Thirty years I waited. Whether they take it today or not, the declaration was made. What's been declared can't be erased.

speaker: narrator
en: The miners' assembly began. Liang Wei led it. At the crater floor. Nearly a hundred people circled. FSP miners. Hellas village people. Nameless people. People who had waited a long time.

speaker: liang_wei
en: I'm making thirty years of data public. Starting today.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Everyone here can take this data. Copy it. Spread it. So MCC can't stop it.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Knowledge cannot belong to anyone. Especially knowledge about this planet.

speaker: narrator
en: People began to move. Data sticks. Copying. Hand to hand. That was how it spread. Not digitally. Person handing to person. The oldest way on Mars.

speaker: narrator
en: One drone lowered. From observation altitude to approach altitude. That was different. Observation had distance. Approach had no distance. There was a difference.

speaker: narrator
en: Then a person came. From the crater entrance side. Not alone. Three of them. Their suits were different. MCC suits. They tried to enter into the crowd.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. MCC representatives. Here to disrupt the assembly.

speaker: lena
en: I can stop them.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Wait. The miners will handle it.

speaker: narrator
en: The miners moved. Without words. With their bodies. They stood before the MCC representatives. Blocking. No violence. Just standing. A hundred standing before three. The MCC representatives stopped.

speaker: liang_wei
en: This metal belongs to everyone. Article 1 of the Mars Constitution draft.

speaker: liang_wei
en: There is no constitution yet. But today these words are the seed.

speaker: narrator
en: The word seed was said. Something not yet existing. But spoken. On Mars things that didn't exist were of two kinds. Things not yet existing. And things that would never exist. What Liang Wei spoke today was on the not-yet side.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. The drone is descending. Need to decide.

speaker: liang_wei
en: No need to hurry. I waited thirty years. A few more minutes is possible.

speaker: narrator
en: There was action. The drone responded. MCC responded. That was all. The rest time would decide. Kepler Crater. Three kilometers deep. Ancient Metal. Thirty years of data. One declaration. Those were colliding here now.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Kepler survived.

speaker: liang_wei
en: For thirty years I looked only at this. Didn't name it. Today it got a name. Kepler Commons.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC sealed the crater. Liang Wei was gone. Where she went was unknown. The thirty years of data was gone too. Kepler Crater was still there. Deep. Dark. It had a name now. A name given by others.

speaker: narrator
en: People came to the outside of the crater. People who had heard. Hellas miners. People from neighboring villages. They looked at Kepler. The crater. Three kilometers deep. Where Ancient Metal was. They said nothing. But they were there.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. Look at those people.

speaker: lena
en: Commons is like this. Even if there's nothing. Just coming and looking.

speaker: narrator
en: From the edge of Kepler Crater CV was watching. That was known. If there was the Sandstone Promise this moment was its test. CV was there. At the crater edge. Hadn't come inside. But was there.

speaker: liang_wei
en: I said Article 1 of the Mars Constitution draft.

speaker: liang_wei
en: There is no constitution. Yet. But I said it today. That's how seeds are planted.

speaker: lena
en: You gave an article number to something that doesn't yet exist.

speaker: liang_wei
en: When you number something that doesn't exist, it begins to exist.

speaker: narrator
en: The data spread. Hand to hand. Out of the crater. To the Hellas villages. The sticks moved. MCC blocked communications. But couldn't stop people walking. On Mars people walking couldn't be stopped.

speaker: lena
en: Liang Wei. Now MCC targets you.

speaker: liang_wei
en: I know. I've known for two years.

speaker: liang_wei
en: I waited thirty years. There's nothing to fear now.

speaker: narrator
en: Seventies. First generation on Mars. Thirty years. Alone. That was the reason for no fear. Being alone for thirty years changes fear. Doesn't eliminate it. Changes it. The object changes.

speaker: liang_wei
en: First time today.

speaker: lena
en: What is?

speaker: liang_wei
en: Seeing together. We saw it together. Today. Kepler.

speaker: narrator
en: CV was at the edge. Cinder was there. Hadn't come inside. That was also the limit of the Sandstone Promise. The promise existed. But it wasn't coming all the way inside. Guarding from the edge. That too was guarding.

speaker: narrator
en:
Kepler Crater turned red. The Martian sun tilted. Liang Wei looked once more. At the crater. At what she had seen for thirty years. At what she had seen today for the first time with others. There were moments when what was alone became shared. That was a declaration. On Mars that was what a declaration was.

Ancient Metal was there. Extraterrestrial origin. Thirty years of data. One name. Kepler Commons. That existed now.

speaker: narrator
en: There was an underground passage. Below MCC headquarters. Built when it was constructed sixty years ago. MCC built it but MCC didn't know all of it. No one knew everything about a large building. That was the nature of large buildings.

speaker: narrator
en: Hellas Central. MCC Hellas Basin headquarters. A large building. Glass and metal. Shining even in the Martian dust. That was intentional. Shining things looked strong. Looking strong mattered to MCC.

speaker: narrator
en: Kenji Nakamura. Grade 3 MCC technical engineer. Five years in the same position. Five years without promotion. On Mars five years without promotion meant one of two things. Incompetence. Or doing something else. Kenji was not incompetent.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a passage entrance. Behind the building. Waste disposal zone. A place nobody came. Even more so at night. That was why it was the meeting place. A place where nobody came. A place to exist as if not existing.

speaker: narrator
en: Hellas labor district. Different at night. In the day people were there. At night fewer. But not completely empty. Night shift workers. Cleaners. People who worked in the Martian night were there. Always were.

speaker: lena
en: Act like night shift. Nobody here should not know us.

speaker: lena
en: There are cleaning suits. Prepared in advance.

speaker: lena
en: Kenji using this route is a first today.

speaker: kenji
en: Not late. Five minutes.

speaker: kenji
en: MCC blocked Liang Wei's data. I backed it up before that. I have it.

speaker: kenji
en: One more thing. MCC has someone inside FSP. Don't know who. Based on communication patterns it's someone senior.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena heard it. The fast person stopped. That was rare. When Lena stopped something heavy was there. The names in the tattoo on her left arm. One of them might have died because of the FSP mole. That was not yet knowable.

speaker: narrator
en: Kenji Nakamura. Thirty-five. Father had been a worker at Hellas Mine 8. After retirement there was no pension. MCC regulations had changed. He had worked thirty years before the change. After the change the pension was gone. That was why Kenji was here.

speaker: kenji
en: Do you know how to receive the transfer?

speaker: lena
en: Tell me.

speaker: kenji
en: Physical sticks only. No communications. MCC sees all communications. They're not unaware of physical sticks but tracking is slower.

speaker: kenji
en: I'll hand it over now.

speaker: kenji
en: You need to protect me. If MCC finds out I'll disappear. From the records. From people's memories. Completely.

speaker: kenji
en: I've been collecting this for five years. For FSP. Because I think you're right. I'm from a miner family too.

speaker: narrator
en: Kenji handed over a package. Small. A data stick. Liang Wei's backup. And other things. MCC internal communications. Five years' worth. That was in the hand. Small. But heavy.

speaker: kenji
en: Three parts inside the stick.

speaker: kenji
en: First, Liang Wei's original data. Second, MCC Kepler plan documents. Third, FSP internal communication patterns. There are clues to find the mole.

speaker: lena
en: Can you find a person from patterns?

speaker: kenji
en: Communication patterns are fingerprints. Different for each person.

speaker: narrator
en: Dangerous information. In two directions. First, this could make FSP stronger. Second, this could create suspicion inside FSP. The same information went two ways. That was the nature of intelligence.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. How we use this information matters.

speaker: lena
en: Finding the FSP mole comes first. Or stopping MCC's Kepler plan comes first.

speaker: kenji
en: Do both. Simultaneously. That way MCC won't know what was leaked.

speaker: narrator
en: A sound from the end of the passage. Not footsteps. The ventilation fan. Sixty years old. But mixed with it was another sound. Small. But MCC buildings carried sound well. Stairs. Passages too.

speaker: kenji
en: You hear that? Someone is coming.

speaker: lena
en: Security. The shift change time changed.

speaker: kenji
en: Need to decide fast. Three minutes.

speaker: narrator
en: The data stick was in hand. Kenji was there. Lena was there. Sound from the end of the passage. Three minutes. That was the time for choices to become choices.

speaker: kenji
en: Do you know what MCC will do if we're caught.

speaker: kenji
en: Record deletion comes first. Then reassignment. To somewhere nobody knows.

speaker: lena
en: Two minutes left.

speaker: narrator
en: Action within three minutes. That was choice on Mars. Choices made with time and choices made without. Both were choices. But different ones.

speaker: kenji
en: We're out. Alive.

speaker: kenji
en: Five years. I waited five years for this.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. The FSP mole story. We have to keep digging.

speaker: narrator
en: Guards in the passage. Kenji was gone. Data was gone. MCC had already known. Moles were on both sides. It was always that way.

speaker: narrator
en: The data was there. Or wasn't. Kenji was there. Or wasn't. One of two outcomes. But in both of them the FSP mole problem remained. That had nothing to do with data. It had been said. Already.

speaker: narrator
en: There was an MCC person inside FSP. Someone senior. Communication patterns. In five years of data. That was what was now known. Two things were unknown. Who. And how long.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena looked at her arm. The names. One of them might have died because of the FSP mole. Park Sung-jin. Mine 7. Three repair refusals. Whether that was coincidence. Or not. Couldn't yet be known.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. I'll tell you. The names on the arm. Some are accident deaths. Some just left. Some — I don't know.

speaker: lena
en: The ones I don't know look different now. After hearing about the FSP mole.

speaker: narrator
en: There was suspicion. That was worse to have inside than outside. Suspicion inside FSP. Suspecting each other. That was what MCC wanted. That was known. But even knowing, suspicion arose.

speaker: lena
en: Analyzed the data. Communication patterns.

speaker: lena
en: The person inside FSP sending information to MCC. There's a pattern. Communications concentrate before and after assembly meetings.

speaker: lena
en: It's an assembly member. Someone from the assembly.

speaker: narrator
en: An assembly member. That narrowed it. But there were five assembly members. Five candidates. One of them. Unknowable. Patterns couldn't identify a person. They only pointed a direction.

speaker: kenji
en: Five years I collected this. Alone.

speaker: kenji
en: Being alone inside MCC. I thought of my father. The day the pension disappeared.

speaker: lena
en: You're not alone now.

speaker: narrator
en: Need to go to Mikhail. Need to report. The FSP mole. Communication patterns. The assembly. That was what was now known. Mikhail would react. Quietly. That was this person's way.

speaker: narrator
en:
Mikhail heard the report. Made tea. The right hand supported the left. He drank it. There was an MCC person inside FSP. That might not be a new fact. On Mars no organization had no moles. Knowing it and not knowing it were different. Knowing meant you could choose.

The tea was warm. That was what could be confirmed tonight. The tea being warm. Beyond that was tomorrow.

speaker: narrator
en: The FSP Assembly Hall. Different from the MCC boardroom. Not sealed. There were windows. The outside was visible. The mines were visible. That was intentional. FSP tried not to forget the outside. That was what the windows were.

speaker: narrator
en: Mikhail had made the windows. When the hall was built twenty-eight years ago. There had been opposition at first. Security concerns. But Mikhail had insisted. He said the reason was simple. We must not forget the outside. That was all. So there were windows.

speaker: narrator
en: Mikhail was there. His right leg was troubled. That was old. Mine accident. The leg remembered it. Today it looked worse. He was sitting. When Mikhail sat in the assembly it was a bad day.

speaker: mikhail
en: The assembly has business today.

speaker: mikhail
en: I've been here a long time. Twenty-eight years since I made FSP. On Mars twenty-eight years is long. My leg knows.

speaker: mikhail
en: There are five candidates for the next chair. You should watch too.

speaker: narrator
en: Five people. Amara Okafor. Yuna Kim. Pak Seung-ho. Dr. Renata Vieira. Thomas Alder. Five sat before the table. Through the window the mines were visible. All five had connections to those mines. That was FSP.

speaker: amara
en: Amara Okafor. From southern Hellas. Eleven years as a representative.

speaker: amara
en: FSP's next step is negotiation. With MCC too. With CV too. Negotiate while fighting. That is how to survive on Mars.

speaker: amara
en: What Mikhail built I will carry forward. But in a different way.

speaker: narrator
en: Mikhail listened. He wasn't holding tea. Today there was no tea. That was different. There weren't many days this man was without tea. His hands were on the table. Both hands. Still. When both hands were still this man was deciding something.

speaker: yuna
en: Yuna Kim. From Hellas mining village. Born on Mars.

speaker: yuna
en: FSP's next step is the Mars-born. People born on this planet must lead this planet.

speaker: yuna
en: My father died in a mining accident. That's the reason.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena looked at Yuna. The names on the arm were visible. Yuna's father's name was there too. Hellas mining village cemetery. Metal plate. Old thing. That was in this room now. A room with names.

speaker: player
en: Third candidate Pak Seung-ho stood.

speaker: pak_seung_ho
en: Pak Seung-ho. FSP economics committee fifteen years. I am a pragmatist.

speaker: pak_seung_ho
en: Execution over ideals. Miners need to eat today. Today's meal over tomorrow's dream.

speaker: renata_vieira
en: Dr. Renata Vieira. FSP medical support team leader eight years.

speaker: renata_vieira
en: The most important thing on Mars is people surviving. Mine safety. Medical access. Those come first.

speaker: thomas_alder
en: Thomas Alder. Former MCC. Three years as FSP representative.

speaker: thomas_alder
en: Inside MCC I understood FSP was right. So I came. Someone who knows the inside is needed for negotiation.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. Alder. From MCC.

speaker: narrator
en: Thomas Alder. There was what Kenji had said. The FSP mole. Communication patterns. Before and after assembly meetings. The pattern pointed to an assembly member. Alder was an assembly member. Three years. From MCC. That was in this room now.

speaker: narrator
en: Three more candidates. Pak Seung-ho was a pragmatist. Dr. Renata Vieira was a medical specialist. Thomas Alder had come from MCC. That was controversial. Could an MCC person become FSP chair. That was another item on today's assembly.

speaker: amara
en: Mikhail. FSP can sit at the negotiating table with MCC. If I become chair.

speaker: mikhail
en: What do you want from the negotiating table.

speaker: amara
en: The safety of miners. Legal protection. Without those there's nothing.

speaker: mikhail
en: Are you sitting with MCC to get those. Or because MCC will give those.

speaker: narrator
en: The difference between Mikhail and Amara. Mikhail doubted. Amara saw possibility. That was the difference between twenty-eight years and eleven years. Those who had seen longer doubted more. Whether that was good or bad was unknowable.

speaker: narrator
en: An environmental alarm sounded. Assembly hall system. Dust storm warning for outer Hellas region. Scale 4. Large by Martian standards. Through the window the horizon was changing. The red was getting redder.

speaker: lena
en: Scale 4. Mining villages are at risk. Especially outer Hellas.

speaker: mikhail
en: Can't stop the assembly. The chair election must happen on the scheduled day. That's procedure.

speaker: lena
en: But the mining villages.

speaker: amara
en: Must postpone the election. Crisis comes first.

speaker: yuna
en: Can't postpone. This is what MCC wants. To divide us.

speaker: mikhail
en: Both are right.

speaker: narrator
en: Two things at once. The chair election. Environmental crisis. Two things coming at once on Mars was normal. But these two coming the same day might not be coincidence. If MCC had known.

speaker: narrator
en: The FSP mole. What Kenji had said. Someone senior. Communication patterns. That was in this room now. One of the five candidates might be it. Or one of the representatives. Or someone around Mikhail. Unknowable.

speaker: narrator
en: Dust began hitting the windows. Scale 4 storm. The lights in the assembly hall flickered. Switching to emergency power. But the windows were there. They were there even as the dust hit.

speaker: mikhail
en: Look at the windows.

speaker: mikhail
en: There are people outside there. Even in the dust. The mining villages. They'll be evacuating.

speaker: mikhail
en: We hold the election. And simultaneously send evacuation support. Both.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a vote. Representatives stood. Called names. On Mars decisions were made with names. Not machines but voices. That was FSP's way. Beings with names deciding with names.

speaker: narrator
en: The dust storm hit the windows. The lights flickered. But the voices were there. Those calling names. They didn't stop. On Mars voices didn't stop. Even when the dust came.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. Look at Alder's voting pattern. Strange.

speaker: lena
en: It matches the pattern in Kenji's data.

speaker: mikhail
en: I know.

speaker: narrator
en: Mikhail knew. That was this person's thing. Knowing everything while not speaking. Making tea and waiting. The way of twenty-eight years.

speaker: mikhail
en: The assembly has concluded.

speaker: mikhail
en: Twenty-eight years ago it started here. There were no windows then. I made them. The reason is simple. We must not forget the outside.

speaker: narrator
en: The assembly reached no conclusion. Five people. Five directions. On Mars too many directions meant going nowhere. Mikhail stood. His leg was troubled. But he stood. That was this man's way.

speaker: narrator
en: The dust storm warning continued. But the assembly ended. FSP's decision had been made. Whether it was good or bad time would tell. For now there was a decision. That was what mattered.

speaker: narrator
en: Contact went to the mining villages. Evacuation preparation. Dust storm readiness. That was what FSP did. Even after the assembly ended the work continued. On Mars work always continued.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. Need to find the FSP mole. Could be inside the assembly.

speaker: lena
en: Today's voting pattern was strange. Thomas Alder especially.

speaker: narrator
en: Thomas Alder. From MCC. Became an FSP representative. That was possible. On Mars many things changed. People too. Affiliations too. But some things didn't change. Things of the past. Things the body remembered.

speaker: narrator
en: The assembly hall was quiet. Dust hit the windows. The storm was coming. Mikhail stood before the window. The mines were visible. Visible even through the dust. That was why the windows had been made.

speaker: mikhail
en: Boss. Stay a moment.

speaker: mikhail
en: About Alder. I knew too.

speaker: mikhail
en: But evidence is needed. Suspicion alone isn't enough. That's why FSP is FSP.

speaker: narrator
en: That was Mikhail's way. Even with suspicion, he waited for evidence. That's how it had been for twenty-eight years. That was what had brought FSP to now. Being right over being fast.

speaker: mikhail
en: A new chair has been elected. Now it leaves my hands.

speaker: mikhail
en: FSP isn't made by a person. It's made by names.

speaker: mikhail
en: The names on Lena's arm. Those are FSP.

speaker: narrator
en:
The assembly ended. Mikhail remained alone. He stood before the window. The mines were visible. The people working in those mines. Their names had made this organization. Names outlasted organizations. He knew that. That was why he had made the windows.

A dust storm was coming. But the windows were there. They would be there even when the dust came.

speaker: narrator
en: New Athens Shipyard. Southern hemisphere of Mars. A place of strong winds. Ships were built where the wind was strong. On Mars ships were spacecraft. Things that went to space. Mars people building spacecraft was rare. Most rode company vessels. This place was different.

speaker: narrator
en: Hagar Volkov. Chief engineer of the shipyard. First generation on Mars. The last generation to remember Earth. A large and quiet person. Hands faster than words. Scars on the hands. Old ones. Old scars on Mars each had their own story.

speaker: narrator
en: Inside the shipyard was a ship. Gaia. Not large. Not a warship. Closer to a freighter. But something was different. Even without seeing the blueprints it was knowable. This ship was for going far. Outside Mars. Beyond Mars.

speaker: hagar
en: FSP came. Good. Need hands.

speaker: hagar
en: This ship is called Gaia. Means Earth. I named it. Don't ask why. Don't want to answer.

speaker: hagar
en: MCC has its eye on this shipyard. They're trying to stop us before Gaia is complete. That's the problem.

speaker: narrator
en: Hagar raised his hand. Toward the ship. The scarred hand. That was the hand that had built that ship. First generation. Seventeen years on Mars. People who remembered Earth while building Mars. This ship was the result of those seventeen years.

speaker: hagar
en: Olu and Mariam designed this ship. Both of them. Took a year.

speaker: hagar
en: Olu is writing a letter now. To Mariam. They planned to ride Gaia together when it was done. Mariam six months ago. Mine accident.

speaker: hagar
en: The letter has nowhere to go. But he writes. Every day.

speaker: narrator
en: Olu Adeyemi was there. Forties. Ship designer. Writing in a corner. By hand. On paper. Writing by hand on paper on Mars was rare. Digital was easier. But this person was writing by hand. That had a reason.

speaker: narrator
en: Olu and Mariam. Two people who designed Gaia. One year. That had been their wedding fund. Hagar said later. They had built Gaia with the money they had saved to get married. Whether everyone knew that wasn't certain. Olu and Mariam had known.

speaker: lena
en: Boss. Do you know? Olu and Mariam put their wedding fund into this ship.

speaker: lena
en: Mariam didn't know. Even not knowing she agreed. When Olu explained.

speaker: lena
en: Don't know if that's love or foolishness. Maybe both.

speaker: narrator
en: Olu was writing the letter. To Mariam. A letter that couldn't be sent. But he was writing. His hand moved over the paper. It didn't stop. He was someone without stopping. That was the person who had built this ship.

speaker: hagar
en: I asked Olu what he was writing. Once.

speaker: hagar
en: He said he was writing where Gaia would go. Where it would travel. What it would see. The things Mariam had wanted to see.

speaker: hagar
en: Mariam had wanted to see outside Mars. Never got to.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC escort vessels were near the shipyard. Two of them. Maintaining a legal distance. But there was something visible at legal distance. MCC always pressured through legal means. That was the most frightening kind of pressure.

speaker: narrator
en: Gaia's completion rate was 87%. Hagar said. Two more weeks were needed. MCC would wait two weeks. Or wouldn't. That was what was unknowable now.

speaker: hagar
en: Thirty-six minutes.

speaker: lena
en: Thirty-six minutes?

speaker: hagar
en: If MCC escorts approach the time we can defend. Thirty-six minutes. Need to decide and move within that.

speaker: hagar
en: The shipyard defense system holds for thirty-six minutes. No more.

speaker: hagar
en: If Gaia is ready to launch within thirty-six minutes we win.

speaker: lena
en: From 87% to launch ready in thirty-six minutes?

speaker: hagar
en: I'm first generation. I can do it.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena went inside the shipyard. The fast person got faster. Checking something. The ship. Connections. Systems. That was Lena's way. Seeing fast. Deciding fast.

speaker: lena
en: Hagar. Status of the main engine.

speaker: hagar
en: 93%. Secondary systems are the issue. Cooling circuits.

speaker: lena
en: I'll do it. Cooling circuits are similar to mine systems.

speaker: hagar
en: Fine. Try it.

speaker: narrator
en: Olu was writing the letter. In the corner. By hand. On paper. MCC escorts were there. Two ships. Thirty-six minutes. That was in this shipyard now. The letter. The ship. Time. They were together.

speaker: narrator
