en: Olu folded the letter. Stood. Looked at Hagar. Those eyes said. Ready. Olu was a ship designer. Not a fighter. But this ship was his. Mariam's too. That had made him stand.

speaker: hagar
en: Olu. Stay somewhere safe.

speaker: olu_adeyemi
en: I'm this ship's designer. I know where is safe.

speaker: olu_adeyemi
en: Something Mariam said. Marriage can happen twice. A spacecraft gets made once. This ship is once.

speaker: narrator
en: Olu's letter was folded. In his pocket. Written with the places Gaia would go. Written with the things Mariam had wanted to see. That was together with Gaia. The letter was with the ship. That was everything in this shipyard today.

speaker: narrator
en: Thirty-six minutes began. The shipyard moved. Hagar's hands. Scarred hands. They directed. People followed. The shipyard moved as if already rehearsed. These people had been waiting for this. For a long time.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena worked on the cooling circuits. Fast hands. Things learned in the mines. The systems were different but the principles were the same. Pressure. Flow. Temperature. Those were the same. Things learned on Mars could be used anywhere on Mars.

speaker: hagar
en: MCC escort vessels are starting to move. Approach altitude.

speaker: hagar
en: Three defense points. North gate. East dock. Roof turret.

speaker: lena
en: Not enough people.

speaker: hagar
en: Always short. But hold for thirty-six minutes anyway.

speaker: narrator
en: Olu unfolded the blueprints. He knew Gaia's weak points. He was the designer. He went to guard the weak points. The letter was in his pocket. That was everything for this person today.

speaker: hagar
en: Gaia survived.

speaker: hagar
en: Olu finished the letter. He says he'll put it on Gaia. The letter goes wherever the ship goes.

speaker: narrator
en: The shipyard passed to MCC. Gaia was there. It would become MCC's. Where Olu's letter was could not be known. Hagar said nothing. When a quiet person said nothing it was quieter still.

speaker: narrator
en: Gaia was there. 87%. Or more. Or complete. Depending. But Gaia was there. Built with Olu and Mariam's wedding fund. It was there regardless of which way.

speaker: hagar
en: Asked Olu. Why he put the wedding fund into this ship.

speaker: hagar
en: He said Mariam told him. Marriage can happen twice. A spacecraft gets made once.

speaker: narrator
en: Mariam had been gone for six months. Mining accident. That marriage could happen twice. But there was no marriage. The spacecraft was complete. That was there now. Gaia. Meaning Earth. The name Hagar gave.

speaker: hagar
en: Olu put the letter inside. Inside Gaia.

speaker: lena
en: Where?

speaker: hagar
en: Beside the navigation computer. A spot Mariam would have liked. Olu said so.

speaker: narrator
en: The letter was inside Gaia. Beside the navigation computer. Written with the places Gaia would go. The things Mariam had wanted to see. Outside Mars. Far places. Things without names. The letter would go there. Together with Gaia.

speaker: narrator
en: Dawn. Light came to the shipyard. Light touched the side of Gaia. Meaning Earth. The name Hagar gave. A name given by the last generation to remember Earth. On Mars those who remembered Earth were diminishing. But the name remained. Names outlived those who remembered.

speaker: hagar
en: Dawn.

speaker: hagar
en: The Martian dawn is different from Earth's dawn. Redder. The sun is smaller. But dawn is still dawn.

speaker: lena
en: Hagar. Do you remember Earth?

speaker: hagar
en: I remember. Fades a little each day. That's why I gave it the name. Gaia.

speaker: narrator
en: What the first generation remembered the second didn't. That was generation. The Earth that Hagar remembered. Yuna and Lena didn't remember it. But Gaia was there. The name was there. Memory remained as a name.

speaker: hagar
en: Olu is there.

speaker: hagar
en: In front of Gaia. Standing. Since morning.

speaker: lena
en: Probably thinking about the letter.

speaker: hagar
en: Or thinking about Mariam. They're the same thing now.

speaker: narrator
en:
Dawn. Light came to the shipyard. Light touched the side of Gaia. Meaning Earth. The name Hagar gave. A name given by the last generation to remember Earth.

Olu's letter was inside Gaia. Or wasn't. That depended on today's outcome. But the letter had been written. On paper. By hand. In the rarest way on Mars.

Mariam was there. In the letter. In the ship. As a name.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Elias Hale prayed while ascending.

speaker: narrator
en: Prayer was not words. It was breath.

speaker: narrator
en: The breath of climbing Olympus. Inside the mask.

speaker: narrator
en: Each breath a prayer. Prayer on Mars was like that.

speaker: narrator
en: The act of breathing itself had to be a choice.

speaker: narrator
en: Olympus. The tallest mountain in the solar system.

speaker: narrator
en: West of the Martian equator. 21 kilometers high. Three times Everest.

speaker: narrator
en: The summit sat above most of the Martian atmosphere. Almost.

speaker: narrator
en: It had taken three days to reach here.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC escort. FSP delegation. CV envoy.

speaker: narrator
en: Three factions walked the same road for the first time.

speaker: narrator
en: The summit station was small. One dome. Three rooms.

speaker: narrator
en: It had been a science outpost ten years ago. Now nobody lived there.

speaker: narrator
en: Someone had brought a table and chairs.

speaker: narrator
en: Mikhail had come up himself to set it up, they said. That sounded right.

speaker: narrator
en: On the table was one sheet of paper and one pen.

speaker: narrator
en: Whether for signing or for notes. Unknown.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale knew why he was here.

speaker: narrator
en: Not a negotiator. A minister.

speaker: narrator
en: His congregation was miners. He held service at the tunnel entrance.

speaker: narrator
en: When they died he called their names.

speaker: narrator
en: Not many could conduct a funeral on Mars.

speaker: narrator
en: So he had come. That was all.

speaker: rev_hale
en: A pleasure to meet you. Rev. Elias Hale.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Chen Weiss. MCC Southern Hemisphere Governor.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Cinder Grace. CV representative.

speaker: rev_hale
en: A minister. Not a representative.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Then why are you here.

speaker: rev_hale
en: As a witness.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena was beside him. The player was there. Amara was there.

speaker: narrator
en: FSP delegation. Five people.

speaker: narrator
en: There were others too. Bodyguards. Aides.

speaker: narrator
en: Fifteen people inside the station.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale looked at them one by one.

speaker: narrator
en: He wanted to know their names. That was his habit.

speaker: lena
en: Let's start negotiating. No time.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: MCC's position is clear. Unified Mars administration. All three factions integrated.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Integration means absorption. CV won't be absorbed.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Integration is cooperation. We should clarify the terminology.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Before we begin.

speaker: rev_hale
en: There are names. We must say them.

speaker: narrator
en: The room went quiet.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen Weiss looked at Rev. Hale.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder Grace placed her hand on the tool belt. Didn't grip it. Just placed it.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena uncrossed her arms.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale took out paper. Folded.

speaker: narrator
en: Old paper. Folded many times. Worn with handling.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Kim Yong-jin.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Mariam Adeyemi.

speaker: rev_hale
en: The three of Sector 7. No names. Unregistered.

speaker: rev_hale
en: The twenty of Zone C. No names.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Hellas Basin miners. Forty-two that I know of. There are more I don't know.

speaker: rev_hale
en: These names come first.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen Weiss set down her tea. First time.

speaker: narrator
en: She hadn't drunk it. But she had set it down.

speaker: narrator
en: That meant something.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder Grace spoke.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: There's Zone 12 too.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: The one MCC sealed off. We lost people there.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Zone 12 was sealed for safety reasons.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Do you know the names. The ones who died there.

speaker: rev_hale
en: That answer is already an answer.

speaker: narrator
en: A sound from outside.

speaker: narrator
en: Not wind. The summit of Olympus had no wind. Too thin an atmosphere.

speaker: narrator
en: Footsteps.

speaker: narrator
en: One bodyguard ran in.

speaker: mcc_guard
en: Pilgrim Arms. External approach detected.

speaker: mcc_guard
en: Four of them. Western slope. Armed.

speaker: lena
en: Where did they come from.

speaker: mcc_guard
en: Unknown. No tracking record.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: They didn't climb up. They were already here.

speaker: rev_hale
en: One of us brought them.

speaker: narrator
en: The room froze.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen Weiss and Cinder Grace looked at each other.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena looked at the player.

speaker: narrator
en: Amara moved to stand by the door.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale folded the paper. Quietly.

speaker: narrator
en: There were moments that required prayer. This was one.

speaker: amara
en: Who does Pilgrim Arms work for.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: The best assassination outfit on Mars. Anyone can hire them.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: MCC did not hire them. I want to be clear on that.

speaker: lena
en: For that to be credible you'd need to go out first and stop them.

speaker: rev_hale
en: There's something more urgent than accountability right now. The people here.

speaker: narrator
en: Pilgrim Arms had a target.

speaker: narrator
en: Not just one.

speaker: narrator
en: Five people in the summit station. The key figures of the summit.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale. Chen Weiss. Cinder Grace. Lena. The player.

speaker: narrator
en: Three guards to protect them. Four assassins.

speaker: narrator
en: Someone could be sacrificed. That was the calculation.

speaker: lena
en: Quick decisions needed. Who stays inside and who goes out.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: I fight outside. My people are there.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: If your people came then you're not the target.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: They're not my people. I could be a target too.

speaker: amara
en: Those who can fight. Come now.

speaker: rev_hale
en: I cannot fight. But I can move.

speaker: narrator
en: Outside the station. The rocky terrain of Olympus summit.

speaker: narrator
en: Almost no air. Thirty seconds without a mask.

speaker: narrator
en: Four Pilgrim Arms assassins came from the west.

speaker: narrator
en: Their equipment was perfect. Trained for low-gravity combat.

speaker: narrator
en: But Amara and the player had ascended Olympus first.

speaker: narrator
en: They knew the terrain.

speaker: pilgrim_assassin
en: Contract is five. Three came out. Good.

speaker: amara
en: I know where the remaining one is.

speaker: pilgrim_assassin
en: FSP girl. Do you have a gun?

speaker: amara
en: No. Still enough.

speaker: narrator
en: The battle at Olympus summit had no sound.

speaker: narrator
en: The atmosphere too thin to carry gunshots.

speaker: narrator
en: A silent battle. It looked like shadows moving.

speaker: narrator
en: Inside the station Rev. Hale watched it through the window.

speaker: narrator
en: He prayed. Without names. There were assassins whose names he didn't know.

speaker: narrator
en: They too were someone's names.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: This summit itself is the target. Someone doesn't want this summit.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Outside the three factions. There is a fourth.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Who is that.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Those who lose when Mars unites. Those who profit from the middle.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Earth-side capital. Martian division benefits them.

speaker: rev_hale
en: I want to know the names. As always.

speaker: narrator
en: Sound from outside the window.

speaker: narrator
en: Not the silent battle. The sound of something breaking.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale looked through the window.

speaker: narrator
en: Amara was down.

speaker: narrator
en: Getting up. Not injured.

speaker: narrator
en: Two assassins were down. Not getting up.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Your FSP people are strong.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Miners. People born on Mars.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: People born on Mars.

speaker: rev_hale
en: The first generation of this planet. People like Yuna. The generation you raised.

speaker: narrator
en: The battle ended.

speaker: narrator
en: Three of four assassins subdued. One escaped.

speaker: narrator
en: The player and Cinder Grace returned to the station.

speaker: narrator
en: Amara had a wound on her left arm. Not deep.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena saw it and said nothing.

speaker: narrator
en: That was Lena's way. Silence when she saw a wound.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Interrogate the subdued ones and the client might come out.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Pilgrim Arms don't name clients. That is their principle.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Principles have exceptions.

speaker: lena
en: That's not the issue now. Continue the summit.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Amara first.

speaker: amara
en: I'm fine. I can sit.

speaker: narrator
en: Five people sat at the table again.

speaker: narrator
en: They had just been fighting assassins.

speaker: narrator
en: But at the table they were negotiators.

speaker: narrator
en: The Martian way. Continue as long as you're alive.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale unfolded the paper again.

speaker: narrator
en: There were names.

speaker: rev_hale
en: FSP's demand is one.

speaker: rev_hale
en: That miners' names be recorded. That accidents be made public.

speaker: rev_hale
en: No empire. No territory.

speaker: rev_hale
en: A person with a name exists even after death.

speaker: lena
en: And improved labor conditions. Medical access. Fair water distribution.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Those follow when names are recorded. Without names there is nothing.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: MCC's position is integration. Administrative efficiency. Resource management.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Worker registration is... something we can consider.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Consider. You call that consideration?

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Changing the entire Mars administrative structure is not a one or two day matter.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: People died because of that structure. Do you consider that too?

speaker: rev_hale
en: Names first. Start there.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale was not a negotiator.

speaker: narrator
en: But he knew how people opened their hearts.

speaker: narrator
en: At funerals. At deathbeds. When children were born.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a common thread. Names.

speaker: narrator
en: When you called someone's name people changed.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen Weiss had a name. Cinder Grace too. That was where to start.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Chen Weiss. When was the day you first came to Mars.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: What does that have to do with anything.

speaker: rev_hale
en: I want to know. People remember their first time.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: ... I was seventeen. Following my father. He was an engineer.

speaker: rev_hale
en: What did Mars look like then.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: ... Red. And empty. Back then.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Cinder Grace. And you.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: I don't tell my story.

speaker: rev_hale
en: You told me about Zone 12. That too is a story.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: I was born there. In Zone 12. That's why I know.

speaker: rev_hale
en: That name should be recorded too. Cinder Grace. From Zone 12.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder Grace looked at Rev. Hale.

speaker: narrator
en: For a long time.

speaker: narrator
en: Then she lowered her hand from the tool belt.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale saw that.

speaker: narrator
en: A small thing. But small things made tables.

speaker: lena
en: Let's move to specific agreements. No time.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Mars integrated worker registration system. MCC can provide the infrastructure.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: If MCC manages it MCC can also delete it.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Make it an independent body. All three factions oversee.

speaker: rev_hale
en: And ministers. Religious communities. Preserving the records as witnesses.

speaker: lena
en: ... That is also a method.

speaker: narrator
en: Negotiations proceeded. For the first time.

speaker: narrator
en: Three factions looked in the same direction.

speaker: narrator
en: Not completely. But it was a first.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale looked at the paper on the table.

speaker: narrator
en: A pen was beside it.

speaker: narrator
en: Names could be written.

speaker: narrator
en: The door opened.

speaker: narrator
en: One subdued Pilgrim Arms assassin was dragged in.

speaker: narrator
en: Amara was holding the arm. With her injured arm.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale stood.

speaker: narrator
en: He walked first toward the assassin.

speaker: rev_hale
en: What is your name.

speaker: rev_hale
en: I'm not asking who sent you. Your name.

speaker: pilgrim_assassin
en: ... Why.

speaker: rev_hale
en: I want to record it. The people who were at this place today.

speaker: pilgrim_assassin
en: ... Ramos.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder Grace watched that.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen Weiss watched that.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena watched that.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale wrote Ramos on the paper.

speaker: narrator
en: An assassin's name and negotiators' names on the same paper.

speaker: narrator
en: A first on Mars.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Tell us the client. Tell us and we'll protect you.

speaker: ramos
en: Pilgrim Arms' principle is...

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Principle put you here. Is principle on your side now?

speaker: ramos
en: ... Earth. Not directly. There's a middleman broker. Talon Group.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Talon. Mars conflict mediation consultants. Them.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Peace is their enemy.

speaker: narrator
en: Talon Group. A name emerged.

speaker: narrator
en: Where there was a name there was existence.

speaker: narrator
en: What existed could be held accountable.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale wrote that name too.

speaker: narrator
en: Names accumulated on the paper.

speaker: narrator
en: The dead. The living. Those who had no names. Those now speaking their names.

speaker: lena
en: Let's draft the agreement. Now.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: MCC agrees to provide infrastructure for the Mars Integrated Worker Registration System.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: CV supports recording of names in unofficial residential areas including Zone 12.

speaker: rev_hale
en: FSP will establish an independent witness network through religious communities. So records cannot be erased.

speaker: lena
en: And water rights. Medical rights. Work hours.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Name recording comes first. Rev. Hale is right. That is the foundation.

speaker: narrator
en: The agreement took shape.

speaker: narrator
en: Each of the three factions didn't get everything they wanted.

speaker: narrator
en: But together they made one thing they all wanted.

speaker: narrator
en: A first in Mars history.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale looked at the window. The sky above Olympus summit.

speaker: narrator
en: Red. As always.

speaker: amara
en: Reverend Hale.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Yes.

speaker: amara
en: When the names are recorded... what comes next.

speaker: rev_hale
en: The names themselves decide what comes next.

speaker: amara
en: How do names decide.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Recorded names are not forgotten. What is not forgotten makes demands.

speaker: narrator
en: Mikhail contacted them. By radio.

speaker: narrator
en: He was below the station. Thirty kilometers.

speaker: narrator
en: He would be drinking tea.

speaker: narrator
en: Two cups. Right hand supporting the left.

speaker: mikhail
en: How did it go.

speaker: lena
en: It worked. We have a draft.

speaker: mikhail
en: Did the names come up.

speaker: rev_hale
en: First of all.

speaker: mikhail
en: ... Good. Then it's done. Come down for tea.

speaker: rev_hale
en: We'll be down soon. Mikhail.

speaker: narrator
en: But there was still something unfinished.

speaker: narrator
en: One escaped assassin.

speaker: narrator
en: Talon Group.

speaker: narrator
en: And an internal traitor.

speaker: narrator
en: Who had called Pilgrim Arms.

speaker: narrator
en: It had come from within one of the three factions.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: It came from inside. Talon knew our location.

speaker: chen_weiss
en: Only a very small number knew the summit location.

speaker: lena
en: It's not from inside FSP.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: That's what MCC and CV would say too.

speaker: rev_hale
en: That problem must not block the agreement now.

speaker: rev_hale
en: Agreement first. The traitor comes after. There is an order.

speaker: narrator
en: The agreement was signed.

speaker: narrator
en: Three lines. As Rev. Hale had wanted.

speaker: narrator
en: First: Every Mars worker is recorded by name.

speaker: narrator
en: Second: Labor accidents are made public.

speaker: narrator
en: Third: Names cannot be erased.

speaker: narrator
en: Signed by Chen Weiss. Cinder Grace. Lena. The player. Rev. Hale.

speaker: narrator
en: And Ramos. The assassin's signature was there too.

speaker: narrator
en: That was Rev. Hale's insistence.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale prayed.

speaker: narrator
en: He didn't remove the mask.

speaker: narrator
en: He prayed inside the mask. With breath.

speaker: narrator
en: Kim Yong-jin. Mariam Adeyemi. The three of Sector 7.

speaker: narrator
en: The twenty of Zone C. The forty-two of Hellas. The nameless ones of Zone 12.

speaker: narrator
en: Now they would be recorded.

speaker: narrator
en: The agreement collapsed.

speaker: narrator
en: After the assassination attempt distrust remained.

speaker: narrator
en: Three factions looked at each other. With suspicion.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale descended.

speaker: narrator
en: Praying. As when he had climbed.

speaker: narrator
en: The names still unrecorded. But the prayer continued.

speaker: narrator
en: If prayer stopped that would be the real end.

speaker: narrator
en: Descending from Olympus Rev. Hale called the names.

speaker: narrator
en: Alone. Inside the mask.

speaker: narrator
en: Kim Yong-jin. Mariam Adeyemi. The three of Sector 7.

speaker: narrator
en: The names below. The names not yet written.

speaker: narrator
en: The Martian sky was red. It always was.

speaker: narrator
en: But descending while calling names the red sky looked different.

speaker: narrator
en: That was the effect of prayer.

speaker: narrator
en: Mars. Red. Always red. Not the observer's first sight. But the first time. Feet touching ground. The surface of Mars. Pressure mask. Oxygen. Numbers. The observer didn't look at numbers. Looked at other things.

speaker: narrator
en: Hellas Central. There were people. People going in. People coming out. People standing. People moving. The observer stopped. Only the observer had stopped. That was this person's nature. Stopping.

speaker: narrator
en: The MCC building was there. Different from before. The observer had seen photos. Before arriving on Mars. Photos and now were different. Whether the building had grown taller or shorter was unknown. But it was different. The people were different. The faces of the people were different.

speaker: narrator
en: The faces were tired. Or vigilant. Or both. Tiredness and vigilance made the same expression. Eyes narrowed. Mouths closed. Shoulders lowered. That was the expression of Mars people. Or the expression of Mars people in this time.

speaker: narrator
en: Someone looked at the observer. While passing. These people didn't stop. Stopping on Mars was a luxury. That gaze said the observer had stopped. A stranger. Someone who didn't know Mars. The observer saw that gaze. That too was a record.

speaker: narrator
en: Next to the MCC building was another building. An old one. Older than the MCC building. In front of it people stood in a line. Waiting for something. Rations or permits or news. The observer looked at that line. It was a long line.

speaker: narrator
en: In the line there was a child. Next to an adult. There were children on Mars. That was a first sight. Not in the photos. The child looked at the Martian soil. The adult looked forward. The child and adult saw the same thing differently. That too was Mars.

speaker: narrator
en: On the outer wall of Hellas Central there was something. Not clearly visible. The observer moved closer. A handprint. Old. Red soil embedded. Someone had leaned on this wall. The reason was unknown. But a hand had been there. The size of the hand. It was a small hand.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer stood next to the handprint. Raised their own hand. Didn't match. Someone else's. Long ago this hand had been on this wall. Where that person was now was unknown. Only the wall remained. Only the handprint remained.

speaker: narrator
en: The mine exterior was visible. From Hellas Central. Far away. There were smokestacks. No smoke. Smokestacks without smoke were different. Different from operating ones. Something had changed. Or was changing. The observer looked in that direction.

speaker: narrator
en: The mine exterior. Equipment. Things not in use. Things parked. They received the dust. Martian dust. Red. The equipment didn't rust. No air. But dust accumulated. If not used dust accumulated. That was the time of this equipment.

speaker: narrator
en: There were miners. At the mine entrance. Miners not going inside. Sitting. Standing. Some were talking. Some were not talking. Their eyes faced the entrance. But they didn't enter. There was some reason.

speaker: narrator
en: Two miners spoke in low voices. The observer heard. Not all of it. Fragments. Accident. Compensation. Numbers. A name. A name was audible. The observer didn't know it. But it was a name. On Mars there were many names. Some remembered. Some forgotten.

speaker: narrator
en: Next to the mine entrance there was a board. A notice of some kind. The observer read it. MCC logo. Date. Numbers. Legal terms. Below that someone had written by hand. A pen. In small writing. The observer bent down. The writing looked like it might be erased. But it was still there.

speaker: narrator
en: The writing was names. Three. Four. Five. Whether that was all was unknown. The space below the notice was small. The names were beneath MCC legal terms. The legal terms were large. The names were small. But the names were there. That they existed was what mattered.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer stood. The miners were still in front of the entrance. Not going in. The observer could have asked the reason. But didn't ask. Asking was intervention. Intervention was not the observer's work. That was this person's way.

speaker: narrator
en: A mining village. Empty. Not entirely. But many houses were empty. Doors were open. Doors with nothing inside. The observer walked. Walked through alleys. Footsteps sounded. No other footsteps. There was no way to know that this village had once been full of people. But it could be known. The way of being empty was different.

speaker: narrator
en: Inside a house there were objects. Some houses. Things left behind by those who left. A cup. A shoe. A photograph. There was a photograph. The observer didn't go inside. Only looked from the doorway. What that photograph showed couldn't be known. But it had been someone's.

speaker: narrator
en: In the center of the village was an open space. Something like a gathering place. There was a table. A broken one. Chairs too. In one corner there were traces of a fire. Ash. Recent and old mixed. People had come here recently too. To an empty village. To burn fires.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer crouched in front of that ash. Didn't touch it with fingers. Only looked. The ash was gray. Gray ash on red Martian soil. The colors were different. That fire had been there the color said. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
en: At the end of the village there were traces of an explosion. An old one. The wall was charred black. The observer walked in that direction. Where the explosion had come from. Whether from inside or outside. Unknown. But it was there. There were traces. Things not yet cleaned up.

speaker: narrator
en: On the charred wall there were handprints. Multiple handprints. Those of people who had escaped. They had leaned on the wall to get out. Those handprints all faced the same direction. The exit direction. All had tried to get out alive. Whether they got out alive was unknown.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a person cleaning. One person. An old person. Looked at the observer. Didn't speak. The observer didn't speak either. The old person swept ash with a broom. Old ash. How long they had been sweeping was unknown. How long they would sweep was also unknown.

speaker: narrator
en: The outskirts of Zone 4. A closed zone. There was a sign. MCC logo. No entry. The observer stopped. Looked at the sign. Behind the sign there was something. Building rubble. Or what had been a building. The entire zone was blocked.

speaker: narrator
en: Next to the sign there was a small stone marker. Not erected by MCC. Erected by someone. Names were carved in the stone. The observer approached. Tried to read the names. Couldn't read them. The writing had been erased. Whether deliberately erased. Or erased by time. Unknown.

speaker: narrator
en: The names on the marker couldn't be read. But the marker was there. Someone had erected it. There was someone who wanted to remember names. There was also someone who wanted to erase names. The marker was between them. Between memory and oblivion. The marker was winning. For now.

speaker: narrator
en: Next to the marker there were flowers. No flowers on Mars. They had been brought. Someone had brought them from Earth. Or grown them on Mars. They were dried. Dead. But they had been brought. For these names. For names that couldn't be read.

speaker: narrator
en: The trace of an explosion was visible in the distance. An old one. Thirty years at least or more. Explosion traces on Mars didn't disappear. No air. No rain. Traces remained as they were. On Earth traces were erased after thirty years. Not on Mars. On Mars traces lasted long.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer looked in that direction. Looked for a long time. Even someone who didn't know what had been there could know that something had been there. That was the nature of Mars traces. They didn't disappear. So Mars was a place with many memories. A place with memories even when no one remembered.

speaker: narrator
en: Night. The labor district. There were lights. Windows. Small lights. People were there. Inside the windows. The observer watched from outside. People inside windows. The observer outside windows. One pane of glass was the difference. But the glass was there.

speaker: narrator
en: In one window there were shadows. Two people. They were talking. No sound was audible. Only shadows were visible. The shadows moved. One person raised a hand. Lowered it. The other watched. That was conversation. The content was unknown. Only that conversation existed was known.

speaker: narrator
en: In the alley a person sat alone. Leaning against a wall. Knees raised. Doing nothing. The observer passed by. That person looked up. Looked down. The observer passed. It was brief. But those eyes were there. The eyes were seen. What the eyes were saying was unknown. But the eyes were saying something.

speaker: narrator
en: In the center of the labor district there was a bulletin board. Flyers were posted. MCC notices. On top of them other things. Handwritten things. Small things. The observer read. Jobs. Missing persons. Names. Meetings. They were mixed. Each person's need was posted there.

speaker: narrator
en: One missing person flyer. There was a photo. A person. A name. A date. Contact information. The observer looked at it. Didn't know where this person was. No way to know. But someone was looking for this person. Someone was searching. That existed.

speaker: narrator
en: From high up in Hellas Central. The observer had ascended. Below was visible. All of it. MCC building. Mining village. Labor district. Mine. Zone 4. They were all in the same place. On the same red surface. Different things on the same surface.

speaker: narrator
en: Other routes were here. As traces. In one route MCC had won. In one route FSP had won. In one route CV had won. But here was different. Here nothing had won. Everything remained. As traces.

speaker: narrator
en: First night on Mars. The observer stood in front of the outer wall of Hellas Central. Where the handprint had been. A small handprint. A marker with unreadable names. An old person cleaning. A missing person flyer. All of those were in one day. The first day. That was Mars.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer watched. That was why this person had come here. Watching. There were things seen on the first day. A handprint. Names. Ash. Explosion traces. Gazes. Those were traces. Traces of other routes. Traces of where this Mars had come from. The observer had to see more. Mars was there. That was everything.

speaker: narrator
en: The northern Hellas. The wilderness. Where few people were. The observer walked. The surface was uneven. The surface of Mars was always uneven. But this area was different. People had dug. Machines had dug. Those traces were on the surface.

speaker: narrator
en: A mining village. There was chalk. On the wall. Names. Kim Yong-jin. Names below. The observer looked. Who wrote them. Why they wrote. When they wrote. Those things were on the wall. Written by people who knew chalk was weak. So they wrote more.

speaker: narrator
en: Below the name Kim Yong-jin there was a date. An old date. Below that other names. Dates. Some names had no date. Whether there had been no time to write dates. Or dates hadn't mattered. There were ones with only names. Only names were enough.

speaker: narrator
en: The names were different sizes. Large names. Small names. Names written by trembling hands. Names written quickly. The names each spoke of their circumstances. Those with space wrote large. Those without time wrote small. Those who were afraid wrote with trembling hands. All of those were on the same wall.

speaker: narrator
en: Near the bottom of the wall there was one name. Low down. It looked like a child had written it. Or like it had been written while sitting. The name couldn't be read. The handwriting was rough. But it was known to be a name. It had tried to say it had been here. The name said that.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer read the names. Couldn't read all of them. Some had been erased. Erased by time. Or someone had erased them. Or part of the wall had broken. But there were names that could be read. The observer read those. Without sound. Not with the mouth. Only with eyes.

speaker: narrator
en: Sandstone Junction. Where three directions split. There was much sand. Martian sand was red. This sand was also red. But there were footprints here. Many. In many directions. Many people had passed through this junction.

speaker: narrator
en: The footprints were each different. Different sizes. Different depths. Footprints of heavy people. Footprints of fast people. Footprints of those who had run. Footprints of those who had walked. Those were in the sand. Sand was erasable. But they were still there.

speaker: narrator
en: In each of the three directions there were traces of flags. Marks of flags planted and pulled. Small holes. The MCC direction. The FSP direction. The CV direction. Three flags had been here. Not now. They had been planted and pulled. The order was unknown. But it was known all three had been here.

speaker: narrator
en: Three holes. The same size. The same depth. The same diameter flag poles. Three factions had used the same flag poles. Or had the same size will. The observer looked at the holes. The holes were empty. Empty holes said more than full ones.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer stood in the center of the junction. Three directions were visible. In the MCC direction there was dust. In the FSP direction there were footprints. In the CV direction there was nothing. Three directions each had different things. The observer watched from the middle. The middle was the place that saw the most.

speaker: narrator
en: The mine shaft entrance. The observer entered. Light decreased. Gloves. Hard hat. Equipment. These should have been there. The observer didn't have them. But entered. Observation could be done without equipment. Or the observer believed so.

speaker: narrator
en: Inside the shaft there were tools. Abandoned things. A drill. Surveying equipment. Metal containers. Those leaned against the shaft walls or lay on the floor. Things used and discarded. Or things left behind. There was a difference. Discarded meant value was gone and left behind meant intending to return.

speaker: narrator
en: On one container a name was carved. An owner. The observer read it. An unknown name. But a name was there. This container had been this person's. The person whose whereabouts were now unknown. Only the container was here. The container stood in for that person.

speaker: narrator
en: On the shaft walls there were scratch marks. Traces of searching for ore. But there were other things too. Stars. Dates. Simple drawings. Someone had waited here. While waiting for ore. While waiting in the shaft. Drew something. Those were on the walls.

speaker: narrator
en: Among the drawings there was a person. A stick figure. A simple one. Next to it was a smaller stick figure. Two people. An adult and a child. In a Martian mine shaft there was a drawing of an adult and a child. What the person who drew it had been thinking was unknown. But they had drawn it. There.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC archive sublevel. The observer entered. Entered without permission. That was not the observer's way. But entered. There were cases where watching crossed a boundary without intervention. This was the first time the observer had crossed a boundary.

speaker: narrator
en: There were documents. Old ones. Early Mars. When MCC was founded. The observer didn't look at them. Didn't want to know their content. But there was something else. Fast footprints. Recent. Two people. One of them had black hands. Ore dust. A miner's footprints in the archive.

speaker: narrator
en: A drawer was open. Empty. Something had been there and was gone. Someone had taken it. Inside the drawer there was dust. A rectangular mark without dust. Where a chip had been. How long it had been there was unknown but a chip had been there. Not now.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer looked at the empty drawer. For a long time. Didn't know where the chip had gone. Didn't know who had taken it. There were miners' footprints. Two people. The chip was gone. Whether those were connected was unknown. The observer didn't connect them. Looked at traces. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC Sector 12 ruins. This too was closed. For a different reason. Not an explosion. It had become unused. MCC had decided not to use it. Deciding not to use something and something being abandoned were different. But the result was the same. No one was there.

speaker: narrator
en: Inside the building there was equipment. Equipment with MCC logos. Things not properly cleaned out. Things that could be used. But they were here. Usable equipment was here unused. What that said was unknown. Budget. Plans. People. One of those or all of them.

speaker: narrator
en: In one room there was a photo. Posted on the wall. Not posted by MCC. Posted by someone later. In the photo there were people. A group photo. People wearing helmets. Miners. Or engineers. The observer looked. Didn't know who they were. The photo was here.

speaker: narrator
en: Below the photo there was a note. A small one. The observer read it. A date. Names. And a short sentence. Zone 12. We were here. That was everything the note said. It was trying to say that they had been here. Nothing more or less.

speaker: narrator
en: Outside Erebus crater. The observer had come. Come from far away. Coming here was not easy. But came. Because it was known there were traces here. Erebus had traces. Old ones.

speaker: narrator
en: Ash from barrel fires. Old. New. Thirty years' worth were mixed. People had lived in this base. They burned fires. After fires went out ash remained. Ash was a trace too. Trace that fire had been there.

speaker: narrator
en: The ashes were layered. Old ones below. New on top. That was time. The layers of ash spoke of time. Someone had burned fires here for a long time. Whether the same person or different people was unknown. The reason for burning fires was also unknown. There was fire. For a long time.

speaker: narrator
en: Inside Erebus base. A small base. Not an MCC base. Something someone had built. Built by one person. The observer looked. There were characteristics of a base built by one person. Only necessities. Nothing unnecessary. Built by someone who knew what was necessary.

speaker: narrator
en: On the table there was a photo. One. Old. Multiple people. Miners. That photo was on the table. No dust on it. Someone looked at it often. Or it had been wiped recently. The photo had been here a long time. The person who was here with the photo had looked at it for a long time.

speaker: narrator
en: Kepler Crater. Footprints. Equipment marks. Analysis tools. Thirty years of traces were here. Liang Wei. The person who came alone. Who was alone for thirty years. Those traces were layered. Thirty-year layers.

speaker: narrator
en: There was one set of footprints. One person's footprints. For thirty years walked in many directions. All those footprints were in this crater. Came alone. Walked alone. Analyzed alone. Those showed as footprints. That it had been alone the footprints said.

speaker: narrator
en: In the center of the crater there was a collection point. There were markings. Numbers. Dates. Layered. The observer looked. Dates spanning thirty years. The same person every year. Every month. Some things every day. Had recorded. Recorded for thirty years to find out what this was. Whether it had been figured out yet was unknown.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer stood at the edge of the crater. The sun was setting. Evening at Kepler Crater. Red sky. Redder crater. Thirty years of traces caught the evening light. Traces were more visible. Or looked more beautiful. The observer didn't record beauty. Only recorded traces.

speaker: narrator
en: There was an abandoned object. At the edge of the crater. An old cup. Without an MCC logo. A personal item. Must have been some miner's. Or an engineer's. The cup was there. No one had taken it. Its owner was not here. Only the cup was here.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer stopped in front of the cup. Didn't pick it up. Only see traces. That was the observer's way. If an object is picked up that object moves. The trace changes. The observer must not change traces. So didn't pick it up. Looked. That was enough.

speaker: narrator
en: But while looking at the cup, thoughts arose. Who owned this cup. How this cup had come here. Why there was a cup at Kepler Crater. There were questions. The observer didn't ask questions. But there were questions. That was the first thing the observer had admitted. That there were questions.

speaker: narrator
en: Came back to Zone 4. The closed place. The marker. The marker with unreadable names. The observer looked again. Nothing had changed. The names were still unreadable. There were flowers. Dead flowers. But there was something different from before. There was a new flower. Someone had come. Had brought a new flower.

speaker: narrator
en: There were traces. Names. Footprints. A cup. Photos. Ash. A marker. A new flower. These were the history of Mars. History not in official records. History that existed only as traces. The observer watched them. Didn't pick up objects. Didn't connect. Watched. That was enough. For now.

speaker: narrator
en: The foothills of Olympus Mons. The observer had come. After the Three Flags conference. How long after was unknown. That didn't matter. What mattered was that a conference had been. And that the observer was now at that place.

speaker: narrator
en: Olympus was vast. The largest thing on Mars. The largest volcano in the solar system. The observer looked up. The summit wasn't visible. There were clouds. Or there was distance. Below on the foothills were traces of the conference site.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a conference site. Traces of temporary structures. Where pillars had been. Where tents had been. Marks on the ground of things placed. Marks of people who had stood. It could be known that three groups had come. Each group had come from different directions. Footprints said that.

speaker: narrator
en: Where flags had been. Three. Holes. The same kind of holes as seen at Sandstone. But larger. Larger flags had been here. More significant. Three holes formed a triangle. The center of the triangle was empty.

speaker: narrator
en: The center of the triangle. The observer stood there. Three holes were around. MCC. FSP. CV. Three directions. The observer was in the middle. The fourth position. The place without a flag. But someone could stand there. The observer was standing there now. Without any flag.

speaker: narrator
en: There was something there. The observer looked down at their feet. It was blood-colored. A bloodstain. Old. The red surface of Mars hid blood. But the color was different. A little darker. There was blood. Someone had died here.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer crouched. Looked at the bloodstain. Not a small amount. May not have been instant death. Or it may have been. The amount didn't tell. What could be known was that someone had bled here. At the conference site. At the center of the triangle.

speaker: narrator
en: There were other things around. Glass fragments. Metal fragments. Things that had broken. The conference had not been peaceful. Or something had happened after the conference ended. Three factions had left this place. Before that something had occurred.

speaker: narrator
en: The footprints had changed. Before and after the conference were different. The incoming footprints had come slowly. The outgoing footprints were fast. Some were disordered. Had run or fought. Directions were different. Not all had gone the same way. They had scattered.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer stepped back from the conference site. To see the whole. Wider. At the edge of the conference site there was something. Small. The observer approached. It was a fragment of a flag. A piece of colored cloth. Which of the three factions it belonged to couldn't be determined. The piece was too small.

speaker: narrator
en: Next to the piece there was another piece. A different color. Another piece. Another color. Three pieces. Flag pieces of the three factions. Those were in the same place. Torn. There had been anger. Or an accident. Or intent. Unknown.

speaker: narrator
en: But there was a fourth piece. The observer found it. A little away from where the three were. A different color. Not the color of the three factions. What color exactly wasn't clear. Old. Hit by Martian dust. But it was different. A fourth color.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer looked at the fourth piece. Didn't pick it up. Looked. Who had brought this. Someone who was not among the three factions had come here. There had been a person who brought a fourth flag. Or someone who had tried to bring one. That person had bled at the center of the triangle. Or not. Unknown.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer stood. Looked up at Olympus. The summit was still not visible. This mountain had watched the conference. Below it. The mountain was old. Older than Mars. Geologically. There had been a conference. There had been blood. There had been a fourth piece. The mountain had seen them. Didn't speak.

speaker: narrator
en: The sun was setting. Evening at the foothills of Olympus. Shadows grew long. The shadow of the conference site also grew long. Bloodstain. Flag marks. The fourth piece. The shadows of those grew long. As the sun set the shadows of traces grew long. That was Mars evening.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer sat. Sat for a long time. Looked at the conference site. Three holes. Bloodstain at the center. Scattered footprints. Torn flag pieces. The fourth piece. What these were saying couldn't be known. Yet. But these things existed. That was known.

speaker: narrator
en: In the evening light the conference site looked different. Different from daytime. Shadows made the traces clearer. Or made them more ambiguous. The same thing looked different depending on the light. The observer knew that. Traces were different depending on when they were seen. That was the nature of traces.

speaker: narrator
en: There were things the observer knew about the conference. Three factions had come. Had tried to reach agreement. Whether agreement was reached or not. Unknown. But traces said something had happened after the agreement. The bloodstain said that. Agreement was not peace. On Mars agreement was never peace.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer walked again. Walked around the conference site. Slowly. Drawing a large circle. To see if things further away were visible. Whether there were traces away from the conference site. The observer searched. There were.

speaker: narrator
en: Ten meters away were lone footprints. Unlike the three groups' footprints they had come alone. Had a size. Adult. Neither fast nor slow. Whether the person of these footprints had joined the conference was unknown. The footprints headed toward the conference site. But whether they had arrived was unknown.

speaker: narrator
en: The footprints stopped. In the middle. On the way to the conference site. Where they stopped there were knee marks. Had fallen. Or had sat. And then went in a different direction. The footprints changed. Became heavier. Were dragged. Had been injured. Or tired. Or decided not to arrive.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer tried to follow those footprints. Stopped. Not the observer's way. Seeing traces. Following traces. Those two were different. Following would lead to finding the end. Finding the end would lead to intervention. The observer didn't intervene. That was this person's condition.

speaker: narrator
en: But the observer thought about whether the person of those footprints was the one who had brought the fourth flag. Tried not to think. But thought came. This person had come with the fourth flag. Stopped in the middle. Went another direction. Couldn't take the fourth flag. That piece remained here.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer came back to the center of the triangle. Bloodstain. The fourth piece. Whether two things were the same person's or different people's was unknown. Couldn't be known. To know would require following. Following was not the observer's way. So it was unknown. That was the price of the observer's way.

speaker: narrator
en: Why had a fourth flag been needed. The observer thought. There were three flags. Mars could be divided with those. Three factions could divide Mars. But someone had tried to bring a fourth. Something other than the three factions. What was it.

speaker: narrator
en: The answer was unknown. That was the observer's way. Not knowing the answer. Seeing traces. Waiting until traces give an answer. Or seeing traces even without an answer. That was what the observer could do. That was all that could be done.

speaker: narrator
en: Night passed. The observer had spent the night here. Near the conference site. That was a first. Spending the night near traces. Wanted to see if traces looked different at night. They did. At night traces were quiet. In the day traces talked a lot. At night traces only existed.

speaker: narrator
en: Dawn light came. Dawn at the foothills of Olympus. Red light came first. Then other lights came. The conference site became visible again. In the dawn light. Looked different. Different from evening and from day. The same traces were different three times. That was the nature of traces.

speaker: narrator
en: In the dawn light the fourth piece looked different. The color looked different. The color that couldn't be determined yesterday. The dawn light told it. It was white. It had been a white flag. The fourth flag was white. What a white flag meant was unknown. But it was white.

speaker: narrator
en: A white flag. Surrender? Peace? Something else? The observer didn't know. White things were rare on Mars. No snow. No flowers. White things were brought. Someone had brought a white flag here. To know what that said more needed to be seen.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer stood. Prepared to leave the conference site. Looked one last time. Three holes. Bloodstain at center. White flag piece. Footprints. Those were here. Would be here even after the observer left. On Mars traces lasted long. No rain. Wind was weak.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer saw one more thing last. Next to the three holes there was a small stone. A stone without a mark. Whether natural or placed by someone was unknown. But it was inside the triangle of three holes. Near the center. What this was. Who had placed it. Unknown. That was everything.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer stayed looking at the stone for a long time. The stone seemed to be saying something. But the words couldn't be heard. The stone didn't speak. Traces had things they said. Traces had things they didn't say. This stone was one of the things that didn't speak. But it was there.

speaker: narrator
en: Eventually the observer picked up the stone. The first time. The first time a trace had been picked up. That went against the observer's way. But picked it up. Under the stone there was something. A small thing. A metal piece. A name was carved in it. Read it. It was a name. A name the observer didn't know. But a name was there.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer placed the metal piece back under the stone. Covered it with the stone as before. Returned the trace to its original state. But the name was known. That was what had changed. The observer knew a name. What that name meant was unknown. But a name was there. That name was here.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer began descending the foothills of Olympus. Slowly. Looking back. The conference site grew distant. Traces became smaller. But didn't disappear. On Mars traces didn't disappear. Grew distant. Became smaller. But were there.

speaker: narrator
en: Descending the observer thought. The person who brought the fourth flag. A white flag. A metal piece with a name carved. A bloodstain. Whether these were connected. Whether from the same person. Or different things. Unknown. But there were thoughts. For the first time the observer had thoughts. Thoughts about connection.

speaker: narrator
en: That was dangerous. The observer knew. When beginning to connect, intervention would follow. With intervention, not an observer. But there were thoughts. Couldn't stop them. Olympus watched the observer from behind. The mountain watched. Had watched the conference. Had watched the bloodstain. Had watched the white flag. And watched the observer thinking.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer stopped. Tried to stop thinking. Couldn't. When traces were seen they became a story. When they became a story they became thoughts. When they became thoughts they became connections. That was the danger of observation. For the first time the observer understood that danger. On Mars.

speaker: narrator
en: Descended the foothills of Olympus. The conference site became invisible. But it was there. Three holes. A bloodstain. A white flag piece. Metal with a name. Had there been a fourth flag. The observer didn't know the answer. That was the observer's way. Not knowing the answer. But this time was different. Wanted to know the answer. For the first time.

speaker: narrator
en: Erebus Crater. The observer had come again. Not the first time. Different from the previous visit. This time there was a purpose. Coming with a purpose was not the observer's way. But came. There was a person at Erebus.

speaker: narrator
en: Watched from afar. There was a person. On the outer wall of Erebus Crater. Alone. Standing. Looking at the crater. The observer watched that person. That person didn't look at the observer. Only looked at the crater. It was Butcher.

speaker: narrator
en: Recognized Butcher. Prosthetic arm. Coat. Wide back. The age was visible in the back. Thirty years were in that back. The observer watched that back. Watched for a long time. Butcher didn't move. Looked at the crater. The observer also didn't move.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer moved closer. Without sound. That was not natural. Moving closer and moving without sound were different. Moving without sound was hiding. The observer hid. That was a first. Hiding one's own existence.

speaker: narrator
en: Twenty meters. Ten meters. Butcher still looked at the crater. Inside the crater. The site of an old mine. Where it had been thirty years ago. The observer also looked inside. Saw the same thing. Same thing as Butcher. But each saw something different.

speaker: narrator
en: Inside the crater were mine traces. Old. More than thirty years. The entrance was sealed. MCC had sealed it. Sealed long ago as well. In front of the sealed entrance there was a sign. The observer read it. Danger. No entry. Date. Old date.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher tried to descend toward the sign. Stopped. Descended. Stopped again. Several times. There was something other than what that body wanted. Whether legs hurt. Or afraid. The observer didn't know. But Butcher tried to descend. Toward the sealed entrance.

speaker: narrator
en: Eventually Butcher descended. Slowly. Along the crater wall. Stood before the sealed entrance. Raised a hand. To the sealed wall. Touched it. With the hand that was not the prosthetic. It had been there. Beyond the sealed wall. Thirty years ago. It was still there now.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer watched. Didn't intervene. Butcher had to be alone. At that place. Had to do it alone. If it were known the observer was there it would change. So watched from afar. Was there but as if not. That was what the observer could do.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher murmured something. Inaudible. Only saw the lip movements. Whether a name. Or a sentence. Unknown. There were words. Those words came out in front of the sealed wall. After thirty years. After thirty years words came from this place. Where those words went was unknown.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher stayed for a long time. The observer also stayed for a long time. Martian time passed. Martian time was different from Earth. A day was a little longer. That made Earth people age a little more on Mars. Butcher had lived thirty years on Mars. Thirty years was a little longer time than on Earth.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher lowered the hand. From the sealed wall. Turned around. Came up. Climbed out of the crater. The observer stepped back. To a place not visible. Butcher came up to the top. Looked far away. At Erebus Crater. Looked again. And walked away.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher left. The observer came out. Stood again at the crater edge. At the place Butcher had been. The observer looked at the same crater. Saw the same thing as Butcher. The sealed entrance. The old mine. The thirty-year-old thing. But it was different. The observer had no memory. Butcher did.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer descended into the crater. On the path Butcher had descended. The same path. Stood before the sealed entrance. Looked at the spot where Butcher's hand had touched. There was a handprint. In the dust. The mark of the hand that was not the prosthetic. It was there. That hand had been there. After thirty years.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer stood next to it. Next to the handprint. Raised their own hand. Next to Butcher's handprint. Didn't touch. Couldn't touch. The observer had no memory of this place. What was contained in that handprint couldn't be known. But the handprint was there. There.

speaker: narrator
en: Hellas Zone 4. The observer had come. Come from Erebus. Come after watching Butcher. Zone 4 abandoned mine. Similar here too. Sealed things. MCC signs. Old things. But here was different. Older than Erebus. Or there was more here.

speaker: narrator
en: Outside the abandoned mine there was rubble. Things that had been buildings. Things that had been buildings thirty years ago. There were walls. Partially. Walls without roofs. On the walls there were names. Not chalk. Old. Scratched. By fingernails. By something sharp.

speaker: narrator
en: There were many names. More than the chalk names. They were scratched. Deeply scratched. Forceful. Hands with fear scratched hard. Or desperation. Desperation to leave a name gave force to hands. That was visible in the names.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer read one name. Kim Yong-jin. Here. A name also in the chalk names. That name was scratched here. Thirty years old. Same name. Different tool. Same desperation. Kim Yong-jin had been here. Thirty years ago. And had left a name.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer stood for a long time before that name. Kim Yong-jin. Name seen in chalk. Name seen in scratches. Same name. Twice. Thirty years apart. That name had lived thirty years. Whether the person who wrote that name had lived thirty years was unknown. But the name had lived.

speaker: narrator
en: Entered the abandoned mine. The observer. Without permission. Second boundary crossing. The first was the archive. The second was here. Crossing boundaries was becoming easier. That was worrying. For the first time the observer had a worry. A worry about oneself.

speaker: narrator
en: Inside the abandoned mine it was dark. There was light. The observer's light. Walls were visible. Ceiling was visible. Thirty-year-old things were visible. Supports. Cables. Equipment. They were old. Thirty years of neglect. But hadn't collapsed. The dryness of Mars had maintained things. No rot.

speaker: narrator
en: There were traces of the strike. Inside the shaft. Graffiti. Slogans. Thirty-year-old things. 'We are people'. 'This belongs to everyone'. 'Zone 4 will be remembered'. Those were on the walls. For thirty years. Because MCC hadn't come inside. Traces remained as they were.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer read those. One by one. Words from thirty years ago. Words written by striking people. They had had things they wanted. Things they feared. Things they claimed. Those were on the walls. For thirty years no one had read them. Now the observer read them.

speaker: narrator
en: Went deeper. The shaft narrowed. More old things. Older things. Things before the strike. Things from when miners worked. Mining tools. Surveying equipment. Those were things used and then stopped. Stopped suddenly.

speaker: narrator
en: Things that had stopped suddenly. Miners had been mining and stopped. There had been a strike. Or an order. Or something had been found. Something had been found. Mining tools had stopped at a specific point. That point was different. The wall was different. The color was different.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer approached that wall. The color was different. Not ore. The strata were different. A mineral. Not a common mineral. The observer couldn't tell. Not an expert. But it was different. That was what mattered. Something different was here. Deep in this shaft. Since thirty years ago.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer didn't know that it was Ancient Metal. Didn't know that name. But knew it was special. Miners had found this. Had struck. MCC had sealed it. Names had remained on walls. People had died. Everything had been because of this. Because of this different color.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer stood before it. For a long time. It glinted. A little. Receiving the observer's light. Not glinting but receiving light in a different way. Absorbed and released differently. That was different. There were minerals that handled light differently. This was one of those.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer raised a hand. Stopped just before touching. Touching would not be observation. Would be intervention. Lowered the hand. But watched for a long time. It was on Mars. Since thirty years ago. It was the beginning of everything. The strike. Death. Names. The sealing. Thirty years. It was here.

speaker: narrator
en: Came out of the abandoned mine. There was light. Martian light. Red. What was inside the shaft was in the eyes. In the observer's eyes. A mineral of different color. It remained in the eyes. For a long time. Even with eyes closed it was there. That was a first sight. Something containing thirty years.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer looked at the abandoned mine from outside. The sealed entrance. MCC signs. Rubble of the wall with names. A marker. A marker with unreadable names. These were together. In the same place. Traces of the event thirty years ago were in the same place. The observer stood in the middle of them.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer had seen what Butcher did at Erebus. Touching the sealed wall with a hand. Knew what that was. It was remembering what had been there. Only someone with memory could do it. The observer had no memory. So did it in a different way. Watched. That was the observer's way.

speaker: narrator
en: Leaving Zone 4 the observer looked one more time. At everything. Abandoned mine. Rubble. Signs. Marker. Flowers. Names. And the different colored mineral deep in the shaft. Those were one story. A thirty-year story. The observer knew that story. Not all of it. But knew it.

speaker: narrator
en: The observer thought. What Butcher had done at Erebus. Touching. The sealed wall. What had that been. The observer wanted to know. Could have asked Butcher. But didn't ask. That was this person's way. But wanted to know. That desire existed. For the first time.

speaker: narrator
en: It was dawn. Outside Zone 4. The observer had spent the night here. Near the abandoned mine. That was the second time. Spending a night near traces. The first was Olympus. The second was here. There was a pattern. The observer was getting closer to traces.

speaker: narrator
en: In the dawn light Zone 4 looked different. The ruins looked different. Night and day and dawn were all different. The same ruins. The observer had seen three times. The same thing differently. That had now become meaning. Not one ruin. Three ruins. Depending on time.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher had been here thirty years ago. Or at Erebus. There was a strike. It ended. People died. Butcher survived alone. Thirty years passed. Butcher came back to Erebus. Touched the sealed wall. That was thirty years. The observer had seen that.

speaker: narrator
en: Whether the observer knew or didn't know. That was unclear. The thirty-year story. The observer was seeing that story. In pieces. In traces. Didn't know the whole. Couldn't know. But was watching. That was what the observer could do.

speaker: narrator

en: Know Helion Dynamics.

speaker: lifang
en: Thirty-eight percent of northern hemisphere oxygen refining. Seven facilities. Until yesterday they were an MCC partner.

speaker: lifang
en: Not anymore. Selling everything. Tomorrow. Before the sale they're siphoning 850 kilotons to headquarters.

speaker: lifang
en: Know what 850 kilotons is.

speaker: lifang
en: A week's oxygen for twelve million in the northern hemisphere. One week.

speaker: lifang
en: The number is too big to feel real. Think about one person. What happens to one person without oxygen for a week.

speaker: narrator
en: Li Fang pointed to a spot on the map. Northern transport corridor. A convoy was passing through there. Already departed, it meant. Not yet arrived. Something could be done in between.

speaker: lifang
en: The convoy has already departed. Thirty-six tanks. Eight trucks. Fourteen guards.

speaker: lifang
en: Dust Storm coming in six hours. Grade 4. All of northern Hellas. When the storm comes the oxygen tanks disappear. Can't be found.

speaker: lifang
en: Recover them in six hours. No tank damage. That's your mission today.

speaker: narrator
en: The fluorescent light flickered again. It hadn't been repaired. No one cared about the flickering fluorescent light in MCC headquarters' briefing room. Other things were more important.

speaker: lifang
en: There's a team. Three people. Four including you. Two vehicles. Weapons are stocked.

speaker: lifang
en: Helion guards will block you. Obviously. You're taking what's ours. If they block you, block them.

speaker: lifang
en: But don't touch the tanks. If a tank is punctured 850 kilotons disperses into the atmosphere. Then all of it is meaningless.

speaker: narrator
en: 850 kilotons. Recover it and MCC acquires the refineries. Fail and it vanishes in the storm. Li Fang looked at you. The briefing room light flickered again.

speaker: lifang
en: Any questions.

speaker: lifang
en: Or none. If none, go.

speaker: lifang
en: One thing. If Helion knows about the storm they'll accelerate. You need to get there before that.

speaker: narrator
en: A last look at the map. Northern transport corridor. Convoy position. Predicted storm path. Six hours. Calculated distance and time. The calculation might be right or wrong. On Mars calculations were often wrong.

speaker: narrator
en: Outside headquarters. Two vehicles. Three team members waiting. All expressionless. Hard to find someone with an expression on Mars. Expressions were a luxury.

speaker: narrator
en: The northern sky was different. Not red. Dark. The direction the storm was coming from. Whether six hours was accurate was uncertain. Martian storms sometimes came before the predicted time.

speaker: narrator
en: Northern Hellas transport corridor. Unpaved road. The vehicle ran. Dust rose. The dust wasn't a good color. Martian dust was always like that. Not good.

speaker: narrator
en: The radio crackled. One team member adjusted the channel. Noise remained after adjustment. Radio on Mars always had noise. You had to listen through the noise.

speaker: narrator
en: Two hours passed. Midway along the transport corridor. Traces of the convoy. Tire tracks. Oil marks. Recent ones. Ahead.

speaker: narrator
en: The northern sky got darker. The storm was accelerating. Faster than predicted. On Mars some things were faster than predicted. The storm was one of them.

speaker: narrator
en: The convoy was visible. Tank trucks. Thirty-six tanks. Moving slowly. Heavy. 850 kilotons was heavy. Guard vehicles on both sides.

speaker: narrator
en: Helion guards spotted the MCC vehicles. They accelerated. Just as Li Fang said. They would block. Blocking was their job. Being blocked wasn't allowed. Six hours had become four hours. The storm was coming fast.

speaker: lifang
en: Full recovery.

speaker: lifang
en: No tank damage. Completed before storm arrival. It goes in the record.

speaker: lifang
en: Not bad. For someone with no Mars experience.

speaker: lifang
en: Next time will be harder. That's Mars.

speaker: narrator
en: The briefing room light flickered. Li Fang cleared the map. The convoy marker disappeared. When missions ended markers disappeared. New markers would appear. On Mars markers always appeared.

speaker: lifang
en: The oxygen vanished in the storm.

speaker: lifang
en: Twelve million short for a week. Remember that number.

speaker: lifang
en: The company will create another chance. Mars remembers mistakes. Know that too.

speaker: lifang
en: Don't make mistakes next time.

speaker: narrator
en: The lights of Hellas Central came on. It was night. The Martian night was long. Inside the building MCC kept running. It never stopped. You were inside it now.

speaker: narrator
en: The storm passed in the north. Hellas Central windows shook. Briefly. The building shook but didn't fall. A sixty-year-old building. It had weathered storms for sixty years. It would weather tomorrow's too.

speaker: narrator
en:
Li Fang stood at the window looking at the northern sky. The direction the storm was passing. What he was thinking was unknowable. On Mars nobody tried to know that. Everyone was busy with their own thoughts.

It was the first day.

speaker: narrator
en: The next mission was an audit. Li Fang pushed a file across. A thick file. No need to ask what was inside. Mine audit report. All MCC mines on Mars were audited quarterly. It was a formality.

speaker: lifang
en: Northern Hellas Sector 7. There was a support collapse three months ago.

speaker: lifang
en: Not in the records. What's not in records we don't know. What we don't know isn't our responsibility.

speaker: lifang
en: Go check. Whether what's not in records truly doesn't exist.

speaker: narrator
en: Li Fang stood up. He took the file back. Left one sheet. Audit checklist. Thirty-seven items. Safety equipment status. Support conditions. Ventilation system. Emergency exit locations. Accident records. Item thirty-seven was last. Accident records.

speaker: narrator
en: Northern Hellas transport corridor. Three hours to the mine facility. Wilderness outside the window. Nothing. The northern Hellas had nothing. That was why they mined there. In a place with nothing, there was something.

speaker: narrator
en: Occasional structures in the wilderness. Exhaust pipes. Old signal towers. Power line supports. All MCC's. There was nothing that wasn't MCC's. In the northern hemisphere of Mars. Nobody asked about ownership. Those who had asked were gone.

speaker: narrator
en: Mine entrance. Iron gate. A guard. The guard checked the ID. MCC audit team, it was said. The guard relayed something on the radio. A short wait. The gate opened.

speaker: narrator
en: The mine facility manager came out. Quick steps. A prepared expression. He knew the audit team was coming. Knowing means preparing. Preparing means hiding. That was the premise of an audit.

speaker: miner_elder
en: Inspector. Welcome. Everything is prepared.

speaker: miner_elder
en: Shall I show you Sector A first. The recently upgraded sector. New safety standards have been applied.

speaker: miner_elder
en: Sector 7 is currently under work so access is difficult. If you come tomorrow.

speaker: narrator
en: Sector 7. An asterisk was made on the checklist. The manager saw it. His expression didn't change. A prepared person. A prepared expression was the most frightening expression.

speaker: narrator
en: Started with Sector A. Checklist. Safety equipment status. Present. Ventilation system. Operating. Emergency exits. Marked. Everything satisfactory. Prepared things.

speaker: narrator
en: The mine elevator descended two kilometers below the surface. As it went down the temperature rose. The surface was below zero but underground was different. Miners knew this difference. Whether knowing it was a good thing was unclear.

speaker: narrator
en: Sector B. Sector C. Sector D. Check. Check. Check. The manager walked ahead. Gave explanations. Stated numbers. Production output. Efficiency. Shift system. The numbers were good. Numbers were always good.

speaker: narrator
en: Miners were working. Some had no safety equipment. No masks. Hands black with ore dust. How much they'd inhaled wasn't visible. Not visible didn't mean not there.

speaker: narrator
en: Written on the checklist. Multiple workers not wearing safety equipment. The manager saw it. His expression didn't change. He said it. Only today. Usually everyone wears them. A few forgot during today's inspection. A plausible explanation.

speaker: narrator
en: Sector E. Passed. Sector F. Passed. Sector 7. The manager stopped. He said next. Said to go to Sector 8. Said again that Sector 7 was under work and couldn't be entered. The asterisk on the checklist was looked at again.

speaker: miner_elder
en: Sector 7 is currently undergoing new support installation. Entry is restricted for safety.

speaker: miner_elder
en: If you come tomorrow you can see the fully upgraded sector.

speaker: miner_elder
en: Today Sectors 8 and 9 are prepared. There is much to see there too.

speaker: narrator
en: Went to Sector 7. The manager followed. He couldn't stop you. Stopping would be more suspicious. Sector 7 entrance. Yellow tape. A sign saying under work. No sound. Under work should have sound.

speaker: narrator
en: Sector 7. Where a support had collapsed. The support had been repaired. But the date of collapse wasn't in the records. No record meant no accident. That was MCC's record-keeping.

speaker: narrator
en: New supports and old supports were mixed. Where the new support had been installed there was evidence. Fresh cement. Around it older cement. The cement colors were different. Different dates.

speaker: narrator
en: Marks on the ground. Scrape marks. Marks from something heavy being dragged. The marks of a stretcher. There was one reason a stretcher would be dragged in a Martian mine.

speaker: miner_elder
en: Inspector. Three people died three months ago.

speaker: miner_elder
en: The support collapsed. Seven thirty in the morning. Thirty minutes after shift start. Before the new shift team had settled in.

speaker: miner_elder
en: Three people. In their thirties. One was supposed to get married this month.

speaker: miner_elder
en: Won't be in the records. Some things disappear before they reach headquarters. Down here everyone knows.

speaker: miner_elder
en: Everyone knows but nobody can say anything. Because if the mine closes there's no work.

speaker: miner_elder
en: I need someone who will put it in the record. I told the manager and he went silent. Silence was the answer I suppose.

speaker: narrator
en: The old miner turned away. His back was small. It was the look of someone who had worked there a long time. The clipboard person wrote something. You didn't look at what they wrote.

speaker: narrator
en: The manager came close. His expression still unchanged. He said the old man had always had complaints. Maintaining accurate records was MCC policy. If there had been an accident it would have been recorded. His words sounded right and not right at the same time.

speaker: narrator
en: The radio was turned on. Li Fang was contacted. The situation in Sector 7 was relayed. Stretcher marks. Fresh cement. The old man's testimony. Li Fang was silent for a moment. There was a length to the silence. Short silence and long silence were different.

speaker: lifang
en: Is there evidence. Or not.

speaker: lifang
en: Testimony isn't evidence. The old man's words aren't evidence. If it's not in the records there are no records.

speaker: lifang
en: You have to decide. The audit report goes up under your name. Not mine.

speaker: narrator
en: Li Fang cut the radio. The radio went quiet. The mine wasn't quiet. Machine sounds. Distant work sounds. Among those sounds the old man was working. Couldn't be seen. His sound couldn't be heard. But he was there.

speaker: narrator
