en: The checklist was in hand. Thirty-seven items. Thirty-six checked. Last item. Accident records. Not checked. There was nothing to check. Or there was too much to check.

speaker: miner_elder
en: Did you put it in the report.

speaker: miner_elder
en: You did.

speaker: miner_elder
en: The dead have names. Three of them. All three had families.

speaker: miner_elder
en: Good that it's in the record. At least their names are somewhere.

speaker: narrator
en: The old miner went back. His back still small. But slightly different from before. Exactly what was different was unclear. Just a little different. On Mars some things changed just a little.

speaker: narrator
en: The sector was still unsafe. The miners had to go back in. They had no other choice. The old man looked at the radio. Said nothing. That too was how Mars spoke.

speaker: narrator
en: The elevator ascended. Surface light returned. Blood-red. The mine stayed below. The miners stayed below. The old man stayed below. The report was in hand. The hands didn't tremble.

speaker: lifang
en: Got the report.

speaker: lifang
en: Sector 7 three deaths. Recorded. That's how you wrote it.

speaker: lifang
en: MCC legal will be in touch. There are procedures. I don't know how it will go either.

speaker: lifang
en: I want you to know what it means to record things on Mars.

speaker: narrator
en:
It was night. The mine didn't stop. The mine ran at night too. Shift system. Miners shifted. The mine didn't shift. The machines didn't shift. Some things didn't stop.

The report was uploaded to the server. It became something that couldn't be undone.

speaker: narrator
en: A summons arrived. Sender: Chen Weiss. Content: 10 AM. 25-Degree Lounge. Brief. In MCC brief summons meant one of two things. Unimportant or very important. This was the second.

speaker: narrator
en: On Mars maintaining twenty-five degrees cost money. A great deal. Chen Weiss's office was always twenty-five degrees. That was the room's name. The 25-Degree Lounge. There was a reason it had a name.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC executive floor. Sixth floor. There was an elevator. But the elevator required a separate key. The 6th floor button was locked. Stairs existed. The stairs also needed a code. The code changed. Weekly. That was why the sixth floor was the sixth floor.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen Weiss was holding a cup of tea. The cup was full. But she wasn't drinking it. This was her way. In the twenty-five degree room the tea wouldn't cool. It could stay like that forever.

speaker: narrator
en: Her parents had been miners. Born on Mars. Second generation. They worked the mines and they died in them. Chen didn't talk about it often. But whenever she held the tea it was there somewhere.

speaker: narrator
en: The window was full-wall. All of Hellas Central visible. A panorama. The city's layers visible. Upper. Middle. Lower. More dust the lower you went. From the window everything was small. The layer where her parents had been was smallest.

speaker: chen
en: Sit down.

speaker: chen
en: I read the report. The audit results. You wrote it.

speaker: chen
en: Take some tea.

speaker: narrator
en: Tea came. The cup was taken. Chen looked at her own cup. Didn't drink. Just held it. In the twenty-five degree air the tea wouldn't cool. That was this room's power.

speaker: chen
en: Three deaths in Sector 7. You put it in the report. That was either courageous or foolish. One of the two.

speaker: chen
en: I don't dislike either. They come from the same root.

speaker: chen
en: Twenty years in MCC. New arrivals who write that in reports are rare.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen looked toward the window. Briefly. Came back. Held the tea. Didn't drink. This repeated. There were things that repeated in this room. Those things made this room what it was.

speaker: chen
en: I'll tell you about my parents. They worked in the mines. Both. I was left alone at twelve.

speaker: chen
en: There was an accident report. The cause section was blank.

speaker: chen
en: That's why I entered MCC. To fill it in.

speaker: narrator
en: She looked at the window. The panoramic window. All of Hellas. The mine district was visible. Small. She held her tea. Didn't drink. Even while telling that story. That said more. More than words.

speaker: chen
en: Twenty-two years. Was it filled? I'm not sure.

speaker: chen
en: Inside MCC you can fill in cause sections. To a degree. Rules can be changed. Checklists can be changed.

speaker: chen
en: But outside MCC nothing can be changed. On Mars. That's what I learned. It took a long time.

speaker: narrator
en: The tea didn't cool. Twenty-five degree air. Chen held the tea. Didn't drink. The conversation continued. But not drinking the tea said more. In this room what was not done was heavier than what was done.

speaker: chen
en: There's a new mission. Kepler Crater. Mineral survey. There's something out there.

speaker: chen
en: A geology team went. The report was incomplete. It needs to be done again.

speaker: chen
en: You're going. There's a reason. You'll understand later.

speaker: narrator
en: Later. When that word was said in this room it had different weight. A later that was certain. Not many people in MCC had a certain later. Chen Weiss was one. That was another name for this room. A place where later was certain.

speaker: chen
en: You'll meet Liang Wei. A geologist. External to MCC. Independent researcher.

speaker: chen
en: Thirty years studying Kepler. A person who spent thirty years in one place on Mars. That person saw something.

speaker: chen
en: Confirm what it is. Then report to me. Not the geology team report. Your thoughts.

speaker: narrator
en: Your thoughts. That was strange. In MCC people rarely asked for your thoughts. It was an organization that wanted your reports. Reports were facts. Facts could be managed. Thoughts were different. Chen Weiss wanting thoughts had a reason.

speaker: chen
en: You can ask why this room is twenty-five degrees.

speaker: chen
en: Standard indoor temperature on Mars is 18 degrees. Seven degrees more expensive. Energy cost. Paid monthly.

speaker: chen
en: Do you know where that money comes from? Miners' work allowances. Contract clause 32. Infrastructure maintenance surcharge. Everyone pays it.

speaker: chen
en: I maintain twenty-five degrees knowing that. That's the meaning of this room. To not forget.

speaker: narrator
en: Tea was in the hand. Warm. Twenty-five degrees. Miners paid for that warmth. Chen kept this room at twenty-five to not forget. That was understood. But whether fully understood was uncertain. On Mars nothing was fully understood.

speaker: chen
en: MCC runs Mars. Mines. Oxygen. Water. Refineries. Without those people can't live.

speaker: chen
en: The issue is how that power is used. Who holds it.

speaker: chen
en: I've watched that for twenty-two years. I know which direction it should go. I need someone to go that direction.

speaker: narrator
en: Quiet. Beyond the panoramic window was Hellas. The city MCC built. From this room everything was small. That was intentional. Distinguishing what should look small from what should not. That was what twenty-two years had taught.

speaker: chen
en: One more thing before the Kepler mission.

speaker: chen
en: The MCC board saw the Sector 7 report. They know your name. Attention isn't always a good thing.

speaker: chen
en: But I called you here. Think about what that means.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen looked at the window. Long. Held the tea. Didn't drink. Hellas was in that window. Small. But from this room it was known that wasn't everything. What looked small wasn't actually small. That was what Mars taught.

speaker: chen
en: FSP knows about Kepler. CV does too. Whoever moves first takes it.

speaker: chen
en: MCC needs to move first. You need to be there.

speaker: chen
en: Cooperate with Liang Wei. But remember where Liang Wei's research goes. The Kepler data belongs to MCC. It's in the contract.

speaker: narrator
en: Contract. Everything on Mars was contract. Oxygen was contract. Water was contract. Mines were contract. But when people died within contracts the cause section was blank. That blank was in the contract. Filling that blank. That was what Chen said without saying.

speaker: chen
en: Finished your tea?

speaker: chen
en: Tea doesn't cool at twenty-five degrees. It's the same temperature whenever you drink it.

speaker: chen
en: That's what this room teaches. Some things don't change with time. That can be power or it can be a burden.

speaker: narrator
en: Held the tea. Drank. Warm. Chen held her cup. Didn't drink. Two cups. One emptying. One staying full. That difference was this room's real name.

speaker: chen
en: Last question. Why did you come to MCC.

speaker: chen
en: No need to answer. Just remember it.

speaker: chen
en: Mars changes people. It makes you forget the reason. People who don't forget that reason last on this planet.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen Weiss was holding the tea. Still not drinking it. Through the window Hellas Central was visible. The city MCC built. From this room everything looked small. She had intended that.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen reacted. Subtly. Lowered the cup slightly. Just slightly. The hand of someone who had held a cup for twenty-two years lowering it. That was the largest movement in this room.

speaker: chen
en: Good.

speaker: chen
en: Go to Kepler. This week. Get equipment from the technical division. Lifang has Liang Wei's contact.

speaker: chen
en: When you return come here. This room. Have another cup of tea.

speaker: narrator
en: Before leaving looked at the window. All of Hellas visible. Upper. Middle. Lower. Dust. Mine. Block C-7. Where chalk names were. From this room not visible. Too small. But they were there. Always there.

speaker: narrator
en: Walked toward the door. Chen was looking at the window. Holding her tea. Not drinking. From behind her shoulders were visible. 22 years of MCC. Miner parents. Twelve and alone. Those things were in those shoulders. Invisible but there. Things on Mars were like that.

speaker: chen
en: You're back.

speaker: chen
en: Mission complete. Data arrived. The report would go to the 25-Degree Lounge.

speaker: chen
en: Take some tea. Today we drink in this room. Both of us.

speaker: narrator
en: You returned. The data was incomplete. Chen would already know. She always did. She would be holding her tea. Not drinking. Tea didn't cool at twenty-five degrees. She could wait. That too was a form of power.

speaker: narrator
en: Twenty-five degrees. It was a temperature. But it was not only that. On Mars maintaining warmth was power. Chen Weiss knew this. She held the tea. Didn't drink it. Tea that wouldn't cool. But that tea was made from miners' allowances. She knew that too. She maintained twenty-five degrees to not forget. That was this room's real name.

speaker: narrator
en: Kepler Crater. Three kilometers deep. A basin within a basin. Where MCC and FSP disputed mineral rights. Whether there were minerals or not nobody knew exactly. That was also why they disputed it.

speaker: narrator
en: 400 kilometers east of Hellas Central. Six hours by transport vehicle. No road. Martian surface. Red bedrock. Dust. Occasionally wind struck the window. Low sound. Martian wind always made low sounds. Different from Earth wind. Earth wind was higher.

speaker: lifang
en: Kepler. Did you read the previous geology team report?

speaker: lifang
en: They said it was incomplete. There's a reason. The geology team didn't descend to the bottom. Not couldn't. Didn't.

speaker: lifang
en: You'll understand why when you see it.

speaker: narrator
en: Dawn. The Martian dawn was different from Earth. The sky was red. Still red at dawn. Redder when the sun rose. Not going from dark to light. Going from red to redder. The first dawn at Kepler.

speaker: narrator
en: Liang Wei was a geologist. An outsider. Neither MCC nor FSP. But she knew Kepler better than anyone. She had surveyed it for thirty years. Thirty years of data was in her head.

speaker: narrator
en: Her research base was at the crater's edge. Small. Two containers. Solar panels. External antenna. Only what was necessary. The space of someone who had researched here alone for thirty years. Unnecessary things disappeared after thirty years.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Look there. The stratum is different. Not ordinary ore.

speaker: liang_wei
en: There's an Ancient Metal hypothesis. Material of extraterrestrial origin. Academia doesn't accept it but I've been watching this for thirty years.

speaker: liang_wei
en: If MCC finds out they'll try to monopolize it. We need to confirm what it is first.

speaker: narrator
en: Liang Wei was talking to an MCC person. Knowing that. Someone who had researched alone for thirty years speaking to someone for the first time. That was felt. Careful. But she didn't stop. Thirty years of waiting kept her from stopping.

speaker: liang_wei
en: First noticed it in 1994. Equipment was lacking then. Couldn't get a sample.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Came back in 2015. The stratum was more exposed. Wrote a paper then. Academia rejected it. Said insufficient data. So I kept coming.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Thirty years. The data is sufficient now. But now the problem isn't academia. It's MCC.

speaker: narrator
en: Descended into the crater. Lifang came along. Lifang was silent descending. Inside the crater was quiet. Quieter than the Martian surface. Wind circled above. Didn't come down into the crater. Deep places were quiet. The quietest things on Mars were in the deepest places.

speaker: narrator
en: One kilometer. Two kilometers. Three kilometers. Descended. The place where the geology team had stopped was visible. A marker. A warning marker. Ground instability. MCC standard marking. Below it no marker. Below it you could keep descending. There was a reason to.

speaker: lifang
en: Warning marker. This is where the geology team stopped.

speaker: lifang
en: Going below is an MCC protocol violation. Officially.

speaker: lifang
en: Liang Wei knows below. There's an unofficial route. I can look the other way.

speaker: narrator
en: Liang Wei went first. Below the warning marker. She didn't hesitate. Someone who had spent thirty years in this crater. This warning marker wasn't a warning to her. It was a guide. Indicating to go further down.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Look here. The stratum color is different.

speaker: liang_wei
en: This color doesn't exist in Martian minerals. Dark silver. Analysis would confirm but the composition is different.

speaker: liang_wei
en: This is what I saw thirty years ago. More exposed now. The crust is moving. Slowly.

speaker: narrator
en: Looked at the stratum. What Liang Wei said was visible. Dark silver. Different from Martian minerals. Mars was red and ochre. This was different. Reached to touch it. Liang Wei stopped the hand.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Not bare-handed. Gloves. Contamination interferes with analysis.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Need to collect a sample. I have tools. I come here often.

speaker: liang_wei
en: The first time I came I touched it bare-handed. 1994. Didn't know then. Know now.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a mineral sample. The color was different. Not like ordinary Martian minerals. Analysis was needed to know what it was. Report to MCC before analysis and it would become MCC's. That was what the contract said.

speaker: narrator
en: Liang Wei was looking at the sample. She had waited thirty years for this. What was in that face was hard to read. But her hands trembled. Slightly. The hands of someone who had waited thirty years.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Extraterrestrial origin. I'm certain. Analysis will prove it.

speaker: liang_wei
en: If this is confirmed the theory of Martian crust formation changes. How Mars came to be needs to be rewritten.

speaker: liang_wei
en: But if MCC monopolizes it there's no research. Only mineral extraction.

speaker: narrator
en: Lifang was beside. Said nothing. That was Lifang's way. A person who said only what was necessary. But his silence now was different. A silence waiting for something. A silence waiting for a decision.

speaker: lifang
en: MCC contract clause 7. Field discoveries must be reported immediately.

speaker: lifang
en: I know that. You know that. Liang Wei knows that.

speaker: lifang
en: So what you do is your decision.

speaker: narrator
en: Above the crater the Martian sky was visible. Red. The sun tilted. The dark silver sample was in the hand. Small. But heavy. The weight of thirty years. The weight of the MCC contract too. Two weights in the same hand.

speaker: liang_wei
en: I know. You're MCC. There's a contract.

speaker: liang_wei
en: I waited thirty years. I didn't think about who it would belong to. Only whether it existed.

speaker: liang_wei
en: But now it exists. And you're here. Now that question exists.

speaker: narrator
en: Sunset. Edge of Kepler crater. The sun was going below the horizon. Martian sunsets were different from Earth. They turned blue. The red sky turned blue at dusk. That moment was brief. But it was there. The first time seeing it at Kepler.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Blue sunset. Only visible on Mars.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Watched it for thirty years here. Every year. This blue only happens in this crater. Other places are different.

speaker: liang_wei
en: I think the Ancient Metal has an effect. The mineral refracts light. That's also evidence.

speaker: narrator
en: In the blue sunset was Kepler Crater. A basin 3 kilometers deep. Dark silver inside. Thirty years of research. MCC contract. Academic rejection. All of that was in this sunset. In the blue light. Light only visible on this planet.

speaker: lifang
en: Report deadline is tomorrow afternoon.

speaker: lifang
en: Chen Weiss is waiting.

speaker: lifang
en: Decide tonight.

speaker: narrator
en: Night came. Kepler's night. No wind below in the crater. Wind above on the rim. Inside the crater and outside were different. Standing on this boundary. Inside and outside. Before decision and after decision. On that boundary.

speaker: liang_wei
en: You won't be able to sleep.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Same for me at first. Thirty years ago. When I first saw this. Couldn't sleep.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Still can't now. That hasn't changed.

speaker: narrator
en: Next day's dawn. Second dawn at Kepler. Red again. From red to redder. The sample was in a pocket. Had been there all night. Decision not yet made. But dawn came. Time for decision came.

speaker: narrator
en: A decision was made. Whatever that decision — Kepler Crater was unchanged. Three kilometers deep. Basin within basin. Dark silver inside. The decision didn't change that. But it changed what came after.

speaker: liang_wei
en: FSP is approaching. There's been a signal since yesterday evening.

speaker: liang_wei
en: They know too. There's a leak somewhere.

speaker: lifang
en: That's why the MCC geology team report was incomplete. They sold it.

speaker: narrator
en: A dust storm. Came suddenly. Martian dust storms came suddenly. Visibility decreased. 50 meters. 20 meters. 10 meters. FSP vehicle signal was approaching. In the dust. Not visible but there. Things on Mars were like that.

speaker: lifang
en: FSP is three teams. North. East. South. Surrounding us.

speaker: liang_wei
en: It's because of the sample. They know about Ancient Metal too.

speaker: lifang
en: Need a decision now. Without site control there's no sample.

speaker: liang_wei
en: Site secured. Sample intact. What happens now is your decision.

speaker: liang_wei
en: For thirty years I didn't think about who this would belong to. Only whether it existed.

speaker: lifang
en: Now it exists. Whose it becomes gets decided when we return to Hellas.

speaker: narrator
en: The site was lost. FSP got there first. Or CV. Either way the sample was gone. Liang Wei said nothing. That was heavier. The silence of someone who had waited thirty years.

speaker: narrator
en: Kepler Crater was still there. Deep and dark. A basin within a basin. Now it was known what was inside. Dark silver. Thirty years of waiting. Blue sunset. Those things were there. Whose it was had not yet been decided.

speaker: narrator
en: Returned from Kepler. Hellas Central. Same city. But looked different. Seen through eyes that had been to Kepler it was different. Three kilometers down. Dark silver. Blue sunset. Those were in memory. Hellas was unchanged. But different.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC's archive was on the fourth sublevel. No elevator. Stairs. MCC favored spaces without elevators. Stairs made people slow. Slow people had time to think. People who thought became afraid. Afraid people kept quiet. That was the purpose of stairs.

speaker: narrator
en: A message arrived. No sender. The content was short. Sublevel 4. Three in the afternoon. Alone. Bring only what you remember. That was all the message said. The message was deleted. But the memory wasn't deleted. Memory couldn't be deleted.

speaker: narrator
en: Descended the stairs. Sublevel 4. 16 flights. The lighting grew darker with each level. Level 1. Level 2. Level 3. Level 4. Lowest. Darkest. That too was intentional. In MCC nothing was unintentional.

speaker: narrator
en: He was there. Forties. Hands black. Ore dust. The kind that wouldn't wash out. Hollow around the eyes. Not the face of someone who hadn't slept. The face of someone who had never known sleep.

speaker: narrator
en: He was standing. Didn't sit. Nothing to sit on in sublevel 4. Archive shelves. Documents packed tight. 30 years. 40 years. 50 years of documents. MCC's memory was here. The irony was this. In this room of memory was where the most things absent from memory were.

speaker: miner_anon
en: No time. Just listen.

speaker: miner_anon
en: The three in Sector 7 were just the start. What I've confirmed alone is seventeen cases. Since 2009. Every MCC safety audit has been falsified. Deaths become accidents. Accidents become normal. Normal becomes excellent.

speaker: miner_anon
en: There's a chip. Original data. No copies. No time to make them. This is everything. If you take this you'll be in danger too. You knew that when you came.

speaker: narrator
en: The chip lay in the palm. Small. A fingertip's length. Seventeen cases. The deaths of Mars since 2009 were inside it. He was trembling. The hand that held out the chip. But the eyes didn't tremble. The eyes of someone who had decided long ago. Those were the heaviest kind of eyes.

speaker: miner_anon
en: Don't ask my name. Knowing it makes you dangerous.

speaker: miner_anon
en: Three of the seventeen were my coworkers. 2019. Ventilation system failure. Three repair requests. MCC didn't approve the cost. All three times. Then the accident happened.

speaker: miner_anon
en: The report had no cause. Personal negligence. That was it. All three.

speaker: narrator
en: Personal negligence. That phrase was in the sublevel 4 air. How many such phrases were in the archive shelves. Phrases that filled cause sections. But not the real cause. MCC's memory was filled with such phrases.

speaker: miner_anon
en: You're the one who wrote the Sector 7 report. I contacted you because of that report.

speaker: miner_anon
en: You filled in the cause section. Ventilation system. A person who wouldn't leave it blank. That's courage.

speaker: miner_anon
en: You're the only one. In MCC. Who will take this chip.

speaker: narrator
en: Those words were heavy. You're the only one. In MCC. To take the chip holding 17 deaths. That was true. Here in sublevel 4. In this thick archive. That was true.

speaker: miner_anon
en: Names are in the chip. Seventeen. From 2009 to now.

speaker: miner_anon
en: Beyond names there are dates. Sites. Repair request records. MCC approval denial records. Everything.

speaker: miner_anon
en: Getting this outside MCC could change things. Even if it doesn't, the record remains.

speaker: narrator
en: The record remains. That phrase had strange resonance in this place. MCC archive. Place of records. But these records were not real records. Falsified records. Deaths without cause. A real record was being passed here in this sublevel. Among the falsified ones.

speaker: narrator
en: A sound came from the stairs above. Footsteps. MCC's building carried sound well. The stairs especially. Two people. Descending slowly. People who descended slowly were not in a hurry. People not in a hurry were more dangerous.

speaker: miner_anon
en: They're here. MCC internal audit. They've been following me.

speaker: miner_anon
en: Take the chip. Now. Deep in your pocket.

speaker: miner_anon
en: I'm here to work. Filing records. Who are you? A stranger.

speaker: narrator
en: He turned. Went to the shelves. Pulled out documents. As if nothing had happened. A person who had waited thirty years became in two minutes someone for whom nothing happened. That was how you lived on Mars. The ability to become nobody in an instant.

speaker: narrator
en: The chip was in the hand. Into the pocket. Footsteps grew closer. Two people. Slow footsteps. On the third sublevel stairs. Now the fourth. Would be visible soon. Had to explain what was being done here in sublevel 4.

speaker: narrator
en: The decision was made. The next moved with that decision. Two people appeared from the stairs. MCC internal audit armbands. They came down. Slow. Not in a hurry. Knew that was more dangerous.

speaker: miner_anon
en: Came to file records. It's weekly.

speaker: miner_anon
en: This person is a new employee. Came for orientation on archive use.

speaker: narrator
en: The auditors looked. As if there was nothing. But they looked. On Mars auditors' eyes always looked. They recorded what was visible. They also recorded what was not visible. That was auditing. Recording absences more than presences.

speaker: narrator
en: Outside. Hellas Central exterior. Night. The chip was in the pocket. Small. But heavy. Seventeen people. Since 2009. Names. Dates. Repair requests. Approval denials. All of that inside this small thing.

speaker: narrator
en: The Hellas labor district was visible. Night. There were lights. Windows. Windows with people. Where miners lived. Where the seventeen had lived. Where their families still lived. The chip was in the pocket.

speaker: narrator
en: A name appeared in an old MCC document. Cinder Grace. Former MCC mechanical engineer. Contract terminated three years ago. Reason: conduct violation. Current affiliation: unknown. There was a photo. The kind of person whose eyes you'd still remember. People on Mars with eyes like that had gone somewhere else.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder Grace. Conduct violation. What that was wasn't in the documents. In MCC documents there were things without reasons. Those things held the most stories. The absence of a reason was the reason. Many things on Mars were like that.

speaker: lifang
en: Was waiting for the report.

speaker: lifang
en: Something happened. It's in your face.

speaker: lifang
en: Before telling me think once more. If I know, then I know. Think whether that's good or not.

speaker: narrator
en: Lifang's words. Whether that was a warning or permission was unclear. That was how Lifang's words were on Mars. Both or neither. Had to decide on that boundary. The chip was still in the pocket.

speaker: lifang
en: The name Cinder Grace came up. In MCC documents.

speaker: lifang
en: Contract terminated three years ago. She leaked safety reports externally. To FSP. MCC found out. Terminated.

speaker: lifang
en: MCC doesn't know where she is now. That's unusual. MCC knows everything.

speaker: narrator
en: In the labor district alley children were playing. Night. Wearing masks. Martian children. Chalk names on the wall. Kim Yong-jin. Names below. People who died in mines. Written by the children.

speaker: narrator
en: The chip was in the pocket. Seventeen names inside. The wall names were there too. Kim Yong-jin. Names below. The names in the chip connected to the names on the wall. The same kind of names. Names not in records. But names written in chalk.

speaker: narrator
en: Outside. Martian air came through the mask. The miner walked a different direction. His name wasn't asked. That was right. Names weren't protection. The chip was there. Small. The history of Mars was in the hand. The history that officially didn't exist.

speaker: narrator
en: No chip. No miner. MCC security filled the stairs. Sublevel 4. A place where footsteps carried well. The deaths since 2009 remained underground.

speaker: narrator
en: Li Fang was waiting for the report. That was his way. What to tell him had already been decided. What remained undecided was what not to say. The difference between the two was large. On Mars it always was. Chalk names were on the alley wall. Wind blew. They didn't erase.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen Weiss read the report. Holding her tea. Not drinking it. Outside the window was the Hellas labor district. A sector MCC built. A sector of people who lived for MCC. The window was thick. No sound came through. That was intentional.

speaker: narrator
en: Information had leaked. MCC knew it. They knew where it came from. And who helped. MCC had a long memory. On Mars there was only one organization with a long memory. That was MCC's real power.

speaker: narrator
en: Vendetta. On Mars that word took a different shape. Not violence. MCC didn't use violence. Violence left traces. Instead they suspended permits. Cancelled contracts. Adjusted oxygen allocations. That was cleaner than violence. And more complete.

speaker: chen
en: Labor district block C-7. The FSP contact network operates from there.

speaker: chen
en: MCC has known that. For a long time. Tonight that block's operating permit is suspended.

speaker: chen
en: There's work for you. Secure the miner database in that sector. Before FSP extracts it.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen held her tea. Didn't drink. Even giving this order. Orders on Mars came like this. In a quiet voice. Holding tea. Without directly threatening. But every word contained a threat. Chen Weiss's way.

speaker: chen
en: There are miners in block C-7. Families too.

speaker: chen
en: If the database is secured their contract renewals proceed. Otherwise renewals are put on hold.

speaker: chen
en: That is MCC's way. Understood?

speaker: narrator
en: Understood. But understanding didn't justify everything. Understanding and agreement were different. On Mars that difference was large. But an order was an order. Refuse an order and there was a next. The next was also MCC's way.

speaker: narrator
en: Block C-7. Night. The Martian night was long. People were in the alleys. Children. Miners' children. Wearing masks. Children wearing masks in alleys. That was what children on Mars were.

speaker: narrator
en: Names were written on the wall. Chalk. Kim Yong-jin. More names below. Several. Not the names of people who died in FSP labor districts. The names of people who died in MCC mines. Written by the alley children.

speaker: narrator
en: The children looked. There was a stranger. No MCC armband. But they knew. Martian children learned that quickly. Who was MCC. By gait. By gaze. By how they looked at the alley.

speaker: narrator
en: The block C-7 server room was there. First sublevel. MCC built this block. MCC knew the structure of every block. Where servers were. Where emergency exits were. Where people gathered. MCC always knew.

speaker: lifang
en: Server is first sublevel. Two guards.

speaker: lifang
en: The FSP contact network is there. Need to secure before they extract it. No time.

speaker: lifang
en: The alley children are watching. Doesn't matter. Focus on the mission.

speaker: narrator
en: FSP contact network. Miners' contacts. A network for sharing safety information. Mine accident information. Danger zone information. Those were in this server. That was what MCC wanted. Without it FSP couldn't reach the miners.

speaker: narrator
en: A name appeared in an old MCC document. Cinder Grace. Former MCC mechanical engineer. Contract terminated three years ago. Reason: conduct violation. Current affiliation: unknown. There was a photo. The kind of person whose eyes you'd still remember. People on Mars with eyes like that had gone somewhere else.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder Grace. The name was remembered. Seen in documents five sections back. Conduct violation. No reason. In MCC documents termination without reason. What that meant was now known. Had leaked safety reports. To FSP. Three years ago.

speaker: lifang
en: You know Cinder Grace?

speaker: lifang
en: Three years since MCC. Was a mechanical engineer. Was a good person. Did good work.

speaker: lifang
en: That's why she was dangerous. A person who does good work and knows MCC's way becomes dangerous.

speaker: narrator
en: Lifang said no more. That was enough. Cinder Grace was someone who had learned MCC's way. And someone who had told the outside. MCC didn't tolerate that. Vendetta came. Contract terminated. Deleted from records. On Mars deletion meant non-existence.

speaker: narrator
en: Children were watching from the alley. Looking toward the server room direction. Children understood faster than adults. What was happening. Martian children grew up that way. As children who quickly understood what was happening.

speaker: narrator
en: In front of the server room. Miner database. FSP contact network. What MCC wanted. But in this database were names. Miners' names. Their families' names. Contact information. What that would become in MCC hands was known. It would become a negotiating card.

speaker: lifang
en: FSP team arriving in two minutes. Detected.

speaker: lifang
en: Secure the server or wipe it. Only two options.

speaker: lifang
en: MCC order is to secure. But you decide.

speaker: narrator
en: Lifang gave the decision to you. That was strange. Lifang was someone who followed orders. But now he didn't give an order. He gave a decision. That difference was large in this alley. Children were watching. Chalk names were there. Server room was there. One minute left.

speaker: narrator
en: Decision made. The FSP team arrived. Into the alley. Children moved to both sides. The children knew situations like this. Knew when to get out of the way. They were Martian children. Fast learners.

speaker: narrator
en: The FSP team stopped. Assessed the situation. They also had to decide. In this alley there were two decisions. MCC's. FSP's. Children were against the wall. Beside the chalk names. That was this scene.

speaker: chen
en: Received the report.

speaker: chen
en: The lights of block C-7 had gone dark outside the window. It was MCC's night. From the 25-Degree Lounge everything looked small.

speaker: chen
en: Small things going dark looked even smaller. But they're not small. That must not be forgotten.

speaker: narrator
en: No server. FSP was first. The children watched from the alley. They knew which side had lost. Children on Mars learned such things quickly.

speaker: narrator
en: On the way back. Chalk names. Kim Yong-jin. Names below. Written by the alley children. Where the children went was unknown. Home probably. The homes where miners' children lived. Homes MCC built.

speaker: lifang
en: You asked about Cinder Grace.

speaker: lifang
en: There's a reason she leaked safety reports. Like Sector 7. Ventilation systems. Things MCC didn't approve.

speaker: lifang
en: When that report got out one miner survived. She knew that. MCC knew it too. That's why they fired her.

speaker: narrator
en: One miner survived. Because of Cinder Grace. That was the conduct violation. MCC's logic. That logic came from the same organization as the person holding tea in the 25-Degree Lounge. Mars was like that. Different logics within the same organization. People lived between them.

speaker: narrator
en: Outside Erebus Crater. Information arrived. Cinder Grace's trace was here. CV territory. A place MCC didn't reach. Or chose not to reach. CV was a different kind of danger. MCC threatened with contracts. CV threatened differently.

speaker: narrator
en: Erebus. There was a reason for that name. In Greek myth Erebus was the darkness of the underworld. On Mars names were mostly from Earth. Names brought from Earth. But Martian landscapes fit those names. Erebus Crater. Crater of darkness.

speaker: lifang
en: No MCC orders reaching here.

speaker: lifang
en: My following you here is a personal reason.

speaker: lifang
en: If you want to meet Cinder Grace go alone. If I'm there it smells of MCC.

speaker: narrator
en: Lifang stopped. Would wait here. That was Lifang's final line on Mars. A place with no MCC order. He was someone who stopped there. That was his way. The way of someone who had lived like that for a long time.

speaker: narrator
en: The chalk names of block C-7 would not be erased by the morning wind. Chalk was weak. But no matter how strong the Martian wind, it could not erase names that had already been remembered. Kim Yong-jin. The names below. The names below that, not yet written.

speaker: narrator
en: The board chamber was completely sealed. No outside air entered. Its own oxygen circulation system. In all of MCC headquarters only the board chamber had its own air. The directors understood what it meant to have your own air on Mars.

speaker: narrator
en: A summons arrived. Brief. Board chamber. 9 AM. There was a sender. MCC Board Secretariat. What the summons meant was still unknown. But it was to be accepted. Nobody in MCC refused a call from the Board Secretariat.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen Weiss was waiting in the corridor. Holding her tea. Not drinking it. She had arrived first. That was a message. This person always arrived first. That was how she existed in this organization.

speaker: chen
en: You came.

speaker: chen
en: You're entering the board for the first time. There are things to know.

speaker: chen
en: Directors don't answer questions directly. The question is the answer. Remember that.

speaker: narrator
en: Seven directors. The table was circular. No head seat. But everyone knew where Chen Weiss sat. That was another form of head seat. The form power takes without marking itself.

speaker: narrator
en: Stopped briefly at the entrance. Voices from inside the door. Low. Indistinct. Seven directors. The most important people on Mars. Their decisions set oxygen prices. Set water prices. Set miners' contract conditions. One door away.

speaker: narrator
en: You entered. The directors looked. Chen didn't stand. She held her tea. Didn't drink it. That was the introduction. That was enough. In the MCC boardroom Chen's silence was a statement.

speaker: chen
en: The board begins. You wrote the Sector 7 report. And secured the Kepler sample.

speaker: chen
en: The directors called you here because of those two things.

speaker: chen
en: It's an evaluation. Whether you're someone who can enter the board.

speaker: narrator
en: The directors listened. No expressions. That was the board's way. Trying to read expressions was pointless. There was nothing to read. When directors showed something it was because a decision had already been made. What was shown in this room was result. Not process.

speaker: chen
en: Director Osei is asking. Sector 7 report. Three deaths. How you knew the truth.

speaker: chen
en: The board already knows. But wants to hear it from you.

speaker: narrator
en: The board knew. It said so. And still wanted to hear it from you. That was this room's test. How you say what is already known. Or don't say it. Or say it differently. Three things were different.

speaker: chen
en: The board has permitted questions.

speaker: chen
en: Director Marchetti — Kepler sample. Ancient Metal possibility. What if FSP already has the information.

speaker: chen
en: These are yours to answer.

speaker: narrator
en: Kepler Crater. Three kilometers deep. Dark silver mineral. Extraterrestrial origin possibility. This was being said in this room. Before the directors. Seven of them. No expressions. But listening. The air in this room was its own. Different from outside.

speaker: chen
en: Director Ryu is asking. How to handle Liang Wei.

speaker: chen
en: Convert to MCC affiliation. Maintain as independent researcher. Or the third.

speaker: chen
en: The third isn't said clearly. But in the board the third is always there.

speaker: narrator
en: The third option. What wasn't said clearly. In MCC that was deletion. Research terminated. Researcher terminated. On Mars deletion took various forms. Contract terminated. Records deleted. Permits revoked. The result was the same. They ceased to exist.

speaker: chen
en: The directors are reacting. Subtly. Setting down pens. Shifting gazes.

speaker: chen
en: Read those. That's the work done in this room.

speaker: narrator
en: Directors waited. Circular table. Seven expressionless people. Chen held her tea. Didn't drink. In this room Chen always held her tea. For twenty-two years. No one had seen her drink it in this room. That was her ritual in this room. Hold the tea. Don't drink. Wait.

speaker: chen
en: Director Osei is asking again. Block C-7. Server. What you did there.

speaker: chen
en: The board knows everything. But wants to hear it from you.

speaker: chen
en: In this room silence is the same as a lie.

speaker: narrator
en: The board knew everything. Block C-7. Server. Decision. They knew and were asking. They wanted to hear it from you. That was a test. The board's test. The oldest kind of test on Mars. Confirming what is already known.

speaker: chen
en: Say it. Before the board.

speaker: chen
en: And if you tell the truth — what the board does with that is the board's decision.

speaker: narrator
en: Directors waited. Seven. Circular table. Chen held her tea. Didn't drink. The air in this room was its own. Sealed. Knew where words spoken in this room went. MCC's memory. Remembered forever. Never erased.

speaker: chen
en: Director Marchetti speaks again. It's been confirmed FSP received leaked Kepler information.

speaker: chen
en: It was an internal MCC geology team leak. That team member has already been handled.

speaker: chen
en: There's information that FSP is sending a team to Kepler. Need to respond first.

speaker: narrator
en: Already been handled. That phrase sounded soft in this room. Board words were soft. But their meaning was sharp. Already been handled. What that meant was something you didn't ask about. In this room. The things not asked made this room what it was.

speaker: chen
en: There's a brief halt. Technical reason. There's a window.

speaker: chen
en: All of Hellas Central visible. A panorama. Block C-7 visible. Small.

speaker: chen
en: Chalk names not visible. Too small. But they're there.

speaker: narrator
en: Outside the window Hellas was visible. MCC's city. The mine district visible. Small. Block C-7 visible. Smaller. Chalk names not visible. Too small. But they were there. Not gone. What was decided in this room went down there. That was what this window said.

speaker: chen
en: Director Ryu requests the final position. How will MCC handle Ancient Metal.

speaker: chen
en: The board has proposed four options. Exclusive control. Decide after analysis. Full announcement. Or freeze.

speaker: chen
en: Freeze isn't an option on Mars. But the board always includes it.

speaker: narrator
en: Directors waited. Chen held her tea. Didn't drink. Twenty-two years in this room. Never drinking it. Nobody knew the reason. For twenty-two years. But today she hadn't yet. Not yet.

speaker: chen
en: A moment.

speaker: chen
en: You know how the board sees you. A threat. A small threat still. But a threat.

speaker: chen
en: I support you. That's dangerous for the board. I know that too.

speaker: narrator
en: The 25-Degree Lounge. Adjacent to the board chamber. Chen was here. Holding tea. Not drinking. This room too was the same temperature as the board chamber. Always twenty-five degrees. That was why the lounge was called 25-Degree. That was where Chen was.

speaker: chen
en: The reason the board is testing you. Because they don't know which side you're on.

speaker: chen
en: Whether it's MCC's side. Or another side. The board always needs to know that first.

speaker: chen
en: I'm asking the same question. About you.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen was asking the same question. The same as the board. But in a different way. The board asked through tests. Chen said it directly. What that difference meant was still unknown.

speaker: chen
en: The board moves to the second session.

speaker: chen
en: Kepler site defense operation. FSP team approaching.

speaker: chen
en: You go. The board has approved it.

speaker: narrator
en: Board approval. The weight of those words was known. When approval came from this room Mars changed. That change went down to the mine district. Down to block C-7. To where chalk names were. Board approval came from here but results were down there.

speaker: chen
en: I've been in MCC for twenty-two years. Today was the first time I drank the tea in this room.

speaker: chen
en: I won't say why. It just was.

speaker: chen
en: The board approved.

speaker: chen
en: Drinking the tea in this room. Whether that had a reason even I don't know.

speaker: chen
en: But today it was like that. That's enough.

speaker: narrator
en: The board deferred the decision. That was a rejection. Board deferrals were always rejections. The tea had cooled. They said tea never cooled in this room. That was one more thing that wasn't true.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen left the chamber. Still holding her tea. But the cup was empty. One person saw it. In twenty-two years nobody had seen Chen Weiss's cup empty. First sightings were rare on Mars. But they happened.

speaker: narrator
en: Hellas Zone 4. Dawn. MCC operational area. Intelligence arrived. CV and FSP were operating a joint base. Outside Hellas Zone 4. They had occupied an old MCC facility. Unconfirmed intelligence. But the board requested confirmation.

speaker: narrator
en: The intelligence was brief. Outside Zone 4. Closed MCC relay station. Multiple CV operatives. And something being moved. What unknown. When today. MCC left many things unexplained. Missions from the board were always like that.

speaker: narrator
en: Zone 4 ruins. A place where there had been an accident thirty years ago. Same zone as Zone 12. Different tunnel. MCC closed it. Three years ago. No reason in the records. There were many things on this planet with no reason in the records.

speaker: narrator
en: Sector 12 ruins. Outer Hellas. There had been an accident here three years ago. The MCC report said equipment failure. But records differed on who wrote the report. Multiple versions existed. In MCC records. Which was the truth was still unknown.

speaker: narrator
en: Inside the relay station. Someone was there. Alone. A woman. Tools hung on her belt. Several. An engineer's tools. Oil on her hands. Working. But no weapon. On the outer plains people without weapons were rare.

speaker: cinder
en: You came from MCC.

speaker: cinder
en: There's only one reason an MCC person comes here. You want to know what I'm moving. I'll tell you. A person. A miner who survived a mine accident. Listed as dead in MCC records.

speaker: cinder
en: Three years ago I was MCC too. That's how I know how they handle things.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder Grace. She hadn't said her name. But it was known. Those were the eyes from the file. Even in the photo it had seemed like eyes you'd remember. In person more so. This was someone who had been through something. It was in the eyes.

speaker: cinder
en: The Sector 7 death report. Three cases. Are you the one who wrote that in MCC.

speaker: cinder
en: That report is why this person is still alive. When it got out we were able to move.

speaker: cinder
en: Then what you do here today is your decision.

speaker: narrator
en: The report. Three deaths in Sector 7. Writing it had meaning here. Cinder knew it. A report from inside MCC. It saved the miner. Someone MCC had processed as dead. It was connected. The report and this person and this day.

speaker: cinder
en: You know Zone 12.

speaker: cinder
en: I was an MCC engineer for six years. I wrote the Zone 12 report. Support beam defects. MCC told me to revise. I didn't. A week later the tunnel collapsed. Eleven people.

speaker: cinder
en: That's why I came to CV. That's my reason.

speaker: narrator
en: Zone 12. Eleven people. Report. Revision request. Refusal. Tunnel collapse. That was Cinder Grace. Someone in MCC three years ago. Someone in CV now. Zone 12 was in between. That was why this person was here.

speaker: cinder
en: What's your reason for being in MCC.

speaker: cinder
en: The Sector 7 report. You wrote the truth. Not the way MCC wanted. Is that part of a reason.

speaker: cinder
en: People with reasons and without are different. On Mars. Here.

speaker: narrator
en: A dust storm came. Mars's dust storm. Visibility narrowed. Outside the relay station was invisible. Through the dust storm an MCC team was approaching. An MCC team that didn't know about this mission. Standard procedure. Neutralize on CV operative detection.

speaker: cinder
en: MCC team coming. You didn't send them.

speaker: cinder
en: The miner is here. A person not in the records. MCC sees and eliminates. You know that.

speaker: narrator
en: The miner was there. In the corner. Hidden. Old. Sixties. Oil on the hands. A miner. Listed as dead in the records. Three years ago. What Cinder had said. Someone processed as dead in MCC records. Alive. Here.

speaker: cinder
en: This person has been hiding for three years. After Zone 12. You know MCC's method of eliminating witnesses. It was that method.

speaker: cinder
en: Need someone to put it in the record. What this person saw. At Zone 12. Someone must write it down.

speaker: narrator
en: A Zone 12 witness. Hidden for three years. Listed as dead in MCC records. Alive. And records were needed. Of what was seen. Cinder was moving for that. With tools. An engineer from MCC. Now a CV person.

speaker: cinder
en: I think you have a reason for being in MCC. Because of the Sector 7 report.

speaker: cinder
en: If that's the reason I think I know what you'll do here today.

speaker: cinder
en: It's strange that you're not trying to kill me. I'm CV. You're MCC.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder wasn't trying to kill. That was the strange thing. When CV met MCC it was battle. Always. But this person was talking. Holding tools. Asking about reasons. What that meant. Still unknown.

speaker: cinder
en: There's a way to fight inside MCC. Writing reports. Putting things in the record. That's the way to fight from inside.

speaker: cinder
en: I didn't know that way. So I went outside. To CV.

speaker: cinder
en: You know the inside way. That's the harder thing.

speaker: narrator
en: The dust storm strengthened. MCC team sounds grew closer. At the relay station's outer wall. Minutes away. Had to decide. Cinder and the miner. The mission. MCC team. And reason. The difference between people with reasons and without.

speaker: cinder
en: Three minutes. Decide within that.

speaker: cinder
en: I'm leaving with this person. If you block me we fight. If not we don't.

speaker: cinder
en: It's your choice.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder waited. Holding tools. The miner was in the corner. Dust storm sounds were heard. And MCC team sounds too. Two kinds of sound. Which was closer. That was what mattered most right now.

speaker: cinder
en: There's a survivor from Zone 12. There was nobody to speak to. For three years.

speaker: cinder
en: If what this person saw is put on record things change. Even before the MCC board things change.

speaker: narrator
en: The board. Circular table. Seven people. Expressionless. They knew. But they wanted to hear it from you. That memory was different here. What this person saw. At Zone 12. If it was put on record. Even before the board things could change.

speaker: cinder
en: I still don't know which side you're on.

speaker: cinder
en: Maybe that's the better thing. Someone whose side is unknown is either the most dangerous. Or the most hopeful.

speaker: narrator
en: MCC team reached the outer wall. Through the dust storm. At the relay station door. Thirty seconds. That was the decision time. Mission. Or reason. Which carried more weight in this moment.

speaker: cinder
en: No time. Now.

speaker: narrator
en: This was the moment. Cinder Grace. Zone 12. Eleven people. Old miner. Records. MCC team. Mission. All of it was in this room. With dust storm sounds. With tool sounds.

speaker: cinder
en: I still don't know which side you're on.

speaker: cinder
en: Maybe that's the better thing.

speaker: cinder
en: When the Zone 12 testimony is recorded contact me. There are things I can help with.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder Grace was gone. The miner was gone. MCC would find out. MCC always found out. The relay station remained closed. There was still nothing in the records.

speaker: narrator
en: Dawn. Outside Hellas Zone 4. The dust storm had passed. Mars's dawn was different from Earth's. Redder. The sun smaller. In the direction Cinder Grace walked was that light. She was someone you felt you could understand where she'd come from. Where she was going was still unknown.

speaker: narrator
en: Olympus Mons. The highest mountain in the solar system. Summit pressure was 0.07 percent of Earth's. Without a mask ten seconds. That was why this place was chosen for the meeting. No one could stay here long. That was the fair condition.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen Weiss arrived first. That was her way. The person who arrived first defined the space. She held her tea. Didn't drink it. Even on Olympus it was the same as the 25-Degree Lounge. That consistency was hers.

speaker: chen
en: I saw this room. Before entering.

speaker: chen
en: Three chairs. One table. No windows. A room without windows on Olympus. That's this meeting.

speaker: chen
en: What is said in a room without windows is real. Not said because of the view through windows.

speaker: narrator
en: Three factions. Three flags. MCC. FSP. CV. Same planet. Different futures. One table. Three chairs. Fewer chairs than people was a problem anywhere in the world. On Mars more so.

speaker: chen
en: Rev. Hale. Cinder Grace. You came.

speaker: chen
en: Today here we agree on the principles of Mars resource distribution. Or three factions divide Mars each in their own way. Only these two things exist.

speaker: chen
en: MCC's position is clear. MCC built the infrastructure. MCC operates it. Whatever the cost, whoever pays it must pay it.

speaker: narrator
en: Rev. Hale sat. Didn't pray. This was not the place for that. Cinder Grace stood. Tool belt unchanged. She had worn it climbing to this summit too. Watching the two of them Chen held her tea. Didn't drink it.

speaker: chen
en: Telling you. This meeting is not a negotiation.

speaker: chen
en: It's intelligence gathering. What Rev. Hale wants. What Cinder Grace actually brought.

speaker: chen
en: Knowing that MCC can decide where to go.

speaker: narrator
en: Not a negotiation. Intelligence gathering. Chen said that. In this room. To you. That was MCC's way. Everything was purpose. The tea too. This room too. The meeting too. All of it was for information.

speaker: chen
en: But today is different.

speaker: chen
en: Cinder Grace brought a photo. Put it on the table. Names. Zone 12.

speaker: chen
en: Something I had locked away for twenty-two years. It's on the table.

speaker: narrator
en: Zone 12. Eleven people. Photo. Names. Chen had known. For twenty-two years. It came to this table. Cinder brought it. With the tool belt. To Olympus. That was why today was a different day.

speaker: chen
en: MCC records show eleven Zone 12 deaths. Correct.

speaker: chen
en: The report exists. The revision request records exist. Today I unlock those records.

speaker: chen
en: When Cinder Grace placed the photo on the table I decided.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen decided. At this table. To unlock the Zone 12 records. For the first time in twenty-two years. Cinder's photo made that decision. That was why today was special. Not information gathering. A decision.

speaker: chen
en: My parents died in the mines. On Mars. Twenty-two years ago. The records said accident.

speaker: chen
en: It wasn't an accident. MCC knew. I found out too. After entering MCC.

speaker: chen
en: Held on inside for twenty-two years. The Zone 12 records were locked. By my hands.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen's story. In this room. Before Cinder and Rev. Hale. First time telling it. Twenty-two years without telling it. Today first. In this room. In a room without windows. That was why this meeting was different.

speaker: chen
en: Cinder Grace. You and I came from the same place. Chose different doors.

speaker: chen
en: Thirty years ago there was someone who called seventeen-year-old Butcher out of the tunnel. My mother. She was a Zone 12 miner. She knew the way. Since then I have been carrying that work from inside MCC.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen said it. That her mother had called Butcher. Thirty years ago. This was the first time it was said in any room. Her mother died. Eight years later. At Zone 12. Twenty-two years inside MCC. And today. On Olympus. In a room without windows. That was what was said in this room.

speaker: chen
en: That's why CV exists. That's why MCC couldn't eliminate Erebus for twenty-two years. Add my mother's thirty years and it goes back even further.

speaker: chen
en: I blocked it. Inside MCC. Every time the board tried to approve an Erebus operation.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen had been keeping CV alive. For twenty-two years. Inside MCC. The eight years before that were her mother. Butcher didn't know. Cinder didn't know. Now they knew. In this room. On Olympus. At the highest point on Mars. That was said for the first time today.

speaker: chen
en: Pilgrim Arms. Four of them are on this mountain. Since this morning.

speaker: chen
en: Those who hired them are inside the board. They knew I was going to unlock the Zone 12 records today.

speaker: chen
en: They're trying to stop me. In this room.

speaker: narrator
en: Pilgrim Arms. Hired from inside the board. To stop Chen. To stop the Zone 12 record unlock. To stop what had been held for twenty-two years inside MCC. That was what was happening on Olympus today.

speaker: chen
en: I'll give you a choice.

speaker: chen
en: If you follow the board's instructions you don't stop Pilgrim Arms. That's standard procedure. For MCC.

speaker: chen
en: If you act independently you protect me. But your relationship with the board ends.

speaker: narrator
en: A choice. Follow Chen's instructions. Or act independently. Follow the board's instructions. Or protect Chen. Those were different directions. On Olympus. At the highest point on Mars.

speaker: chen
en: Twenty-two years. To get here.

speaker: chen
en: When the Zone 12 records are unlocked the board changes. MCC changes. Mars changes.

speaker: chen
en: That's the reason for twenty-two years.

speaker: narrator
en: Outside Olympus. Pilgrim Arms four were moving. Two east. Two west. Along the base's outer wall. After Chen. To stop the Zone 12 record unlock. Hired by the board. Inside MCC.

speaker: chen
en: Cinder Grace went to stop the eastern side. With tools.

speaker: chen
en: The west remains. You decide.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder went out. With tools. On Olympus. At the highest point in the solar system. Tool sounds. That was the answer to this situation. Cinder's way. Fixing with tools. That went from this room to the outside.

speaker: chen
en: The board is trying to stop me. For the first time in twenty-two years.

speaker: chen
en: That's proof I'm going in the right direction.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen held her tea. Didn't drink it. In this room. Twenty-two years without drinking. But today. A little. She drank. Zone 12 photo was on the table. What Cinder brought. It was in this room. That was why today was different.

speaker: chen
en: An agreement is needed. Today. Three factions. The Zone 12 names must be in this agreement.

speaker: chen
en: That's what the board is trying to stop. Names appearing in official documents.

speaker: chen
en: It's your decision.

speaker: narrator
en: Names appearing in official documents. That was what the board was trying to stop. What had been locked away for twenty-two years. That was trying to open in this room today. And Pilgrim Arms had come to stop it. On the board's order.

speaker: chen
en: The western two are approaching. Reaching this room within one minute.

speaker: chen
en: I'll sign the agreement. While you stop them.

speaker: narrator
en: Chen picked up the pen. Before the agreement. The agreement with names. Zone 12. Needing the signatures of three factions. One of them. That was about to happen. Sounds from the west. Close.

speaker: narrator
en: The agreement was signed. Three factions. Three signatures. Chen's was last. Before taking the pen she set down her tea. She signed with both hands. The right supporting the left. That was not her way. But today it was. This signature was worth that.

speaker: narrator
en: The meeting didn't end. A meeting that didn't end was a collapse. Three factions went their separate ways. Olympus remained. Mountains always remained. Even when people left. Even without agreement. Zone 12 names remained locked. But Cinder had picked up her tools. That was different.

speaker: narrator
en: Descending from Olympus. All of Mars was visible. Red. Below was Hellas. MCC's city. Smaller still was block C-7. The chalk names. Coming down they would be large again. That was what this mountain taught. Small things became large again on the way down.

speaker: narrator
en: Hellas Central. Largest settlement in the southern hemisphere. Population four thousand. Half were miners. The rest lived off those miners. There was law. MCC had made it. That was the law.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a rumor. Something south. It had a name. CV. Crimson Warlords. Everyone who mentioned it said something different. Some called them raiders. Some called them survivors. Some said nothing at all.

speaker: narrator
en: You had been in this bar for two days. You planned to stay until the money ran out. When the money was gone you'd think about what came next. That was how you had lived until now.

speaker: bartender
en: People have been going south. Three this month alone.

speaker: bartender
en: None came back.

speaker: bartender
en: Don't know if they're dead or if they stayed. Don't know if there's a difference.

speaker: narrator
en: That stuck. Dead or staying. Maybe no difference. But if there was a difference — couldn't tell if staying was worse or better.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a man in the corner. Scars on his hands. Not a miner's hands. Different scars. His eyes met yours first. He didn't look away. That was strange. No one in this bar held your gaze.

speaker: stranger
en: You heard about the south.

speaker: stranger
en: You don't go find it. It finds you. Good to know that.

speaker: narrator
en: The man said nothing more. Drank his drink. When the glass was empty he stood. Left without looking back. His steps were quiet. Not the walk of someone from this city.

speaker: narrator
en: Next morning. You were walking south. Didn't know why. Just walking as if there was a reason. The south of Mars was colder. The ground was redder. The air thinner.

speaker: narrator
en: No map. Only direction. South. Only rumor. Erebus. Only a name. Crater. That was all. That was how you got here.

speaker: narrator
en: Hellas Central disappeared from view. Only plains remained. Vast. Empty of people. On Mars empty places were dangerous. No help. But nothing to harm you either. That was the difference between danger and freedom.

speaker: narrator
en: Three hours walking. Not hungry. Cold. Day on Mars was minus thirty degrees. Night approached minus one hundred. You knew that. Didn't stop.

speaker: narrator
en: The sun tilted. The Martian sunset was different. Blue. Earth sunsets were red. Martian sunsets were blue. Those who knew that said it felt strange the first time they saw it. Now it felt natural to you. Couldn't tell if you had changed or adapted to Mars.

speaker: narrator
en: Sound from behind. Footsteps. More than one. Stopped. Didn't turn around. Nowhere to run. No reason to fight. Just waited. That was all there was to do in this situation.

speaker: cv_scout_1
en: Alone?

speaker: player
en: Yes.

speaker: cv_scout_1
en: Where from.

speaker: player
en: Hellas Central.

speaker: cv_scout_2
en: Armed?

speaker: player
en: A knife.

speaker: narrator
en: Two of them. Armed. Faces covered. Only eyes visible. Those eyes studied you for a long time. Top to bottom. Bottom to top. Couldn't tell what they were looking for. Whether you were dangerous. Useful. Or should disappear.

speaker: cv_scout_1
en: Why south.

speaker: player
en: There was a rumor.

speaker: cv_scout_1
en: What rumor.

speaker: player
en: That you don't go find it. It finds you.

speaker: narrator
en: The two looked at each other. Said nothing. But something was decided. You could see it. In faces where only eyes were visible. Eyes that spoke.

speaker: cv_scout_1
en: Blindfold.

speaker: player
en: Why.

speaker: cv_scout_1
en: That's how you get there. Don't like it, don't come.

speaker: narrator
en: The blindfold went on. Light disappeared. Only sounds remained. Wind. Footsteps. The two and your own. No way to tell direction. No way to know where. But you walked. That was what could be done now.

speaker: narrator
en: Didn't know how long. Felt the terrain change through the feet. From flat to slope. Downward. A sense of deepening. Descending into a crater. You could tell.

speaker: narrator
en: The air changed. Colder. But no wind. Inside the crater. Walls blocked the wind. Sound changed. Echo. Deep place. Firelight felt through the blindfold.

speaker: narrator
en: Stopped. Footsteps stopped. Blindfold removed. Eyes took time to adjust. Firelight. A large fire. Burning at the crater floor. People. Many of them. All watching.

speaker: narrator
en: No one spoke. That was strange. A place where someone arriving brought no words. But not dangerous. Not yet. You could tell.

speaker: narrator
en: A man sat before the fire. Large and heavy. A prosthetic. Left arm. Old mining-grade. He lifted his eyes from the fire. Looked at you. For a long time.

speaker: butcher_vasquez
en: Still alive.

speaker: butcher_vasquez
en: You heard the rumor. That's enough.

speaker: narrator
en: That was all. No welcome. No warning. The fire just burned. People went about their work. You stood before the fire. Not warm. Fire burning but not warm. Minus one hundred degrees.

speaker: narrator
en: This was CV. Fire was here. Burning. But not warm. That was this place. Didn't take long to understand. Already knew it. Maybe that was why you'd come this far.

speaker: narrator
en: Butcher Vasquez looked back at the fire. The conversation was over. Or it had never begun. Someone else appeared. A woman. Tool belt on her arm. Sharp eyes.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Rough hands.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: What have you been doing.

speaker: player
en: Surviving.

speaker: cinder_grace
en: Do that here and you'll be fine.

speaker: narrator
en: Cinder Grace turned away. Touched her tools. The ones on the belt. A habit. You stayed before the fire. It burned. Not warm. But burning.

speaker: narrator
en: Looked around. People. Each with their own wounds. People whose names you didn't know. But people in the same place. People around a fire. Around a fire that wasn't warm.

speaker: narrator
en: Night was coming. The sky above the crater darkened. Stars came out. Martian stars. Same stars as seen from Earth but different stars. Stars seen from here. That made them different.

speaker: narrator
en: Someone handed over a blanket. No words. Didn't know their name. Just handed it over. You took it. That was the first exchange here. Something done without words. That was CV.

speaker: narrator
en: Fire burned. Not warm. But a fire that had not gone out in thirty years. You were here. The first night. Couldn't tell if this was a choice or a discovery. Maybe this was a place where those two things were the same.

speaker: narrator
en:
2087. Year 17 of Mars settlement.
New Athens — free settlement in Hellas Basin. Population 4,200.
A town built by hand, not by a corporation.

speaker: narrator
en:
Nine months from Earth departure. Three days after Mars atmospheric entry.
From above Hellas Basin the surface was visible for the first time.
Red. Redder than expected. Not like the photos.

speaker: narrator
en:
You had just arrived.
One sheet of paper with a green FSP stamp.
That was all that proved you belonged here.

speaker: narrator
en: People were at the landing pad. Most were miners. Rough hands. Eyes were different. Eyes not seen on Earth. The eyes of someone who had endured a long time. But there was light. Light not yet extinguished.

speaker: narrator
en: Hellas labor district. Too narrow to call a village. Too human-smelling to call a base. Made by the first Mars generation. Added to by the next. And the one after. Seventeen years of layers.

speaker: narrator
en: Names were on the walls. Written in chalk. Miners' names. Dates. Some were old. Some were new. Chalk was weak. But they were there.

speaker: lena
en: Fresh face. You smell like Earth.

speaker: lena
en: Don't be surprised. Not a bad thing. Everyone's like that at first. After six months you smell like Mars.

speaker: lena
en: What's your name? Ah, don't need to ask. Heard from Amara. Said you're an FSP referral.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena Torres. A tattoo on the left arm. Names. Wrist to shoulder. What it was wasn't yet known. But that it was important was known. People engrave important things on their bodies.

speaker: narrator
en: There was a corridor. Narrow. Leading inward. Lena walked ahead. A fast person. Fast walk, fast talk, fast judgment. Many such people in this village. On Mars being slow was expensive.

speaker: narrator
en: A room. Small. One window. Through the window Mars was visible. Red plains. Beyond that something was there. A mine. Lights still on. Night shift.

speaker: narrator
en: The sound of tea being made. From inside the room. And there was that person. Someone standing with their back turned. Shoulders not wide. Not tall. But that back was the largest thing in the room.

speaker: mikhail
en: You made it. Cold? Sorry. Two wind turbines broke down. The hangar is running at 30% capacity.

speaker: mikhail
en: Have some tea. This is real tea. Grown from seeds brought from Earth. The only tea grown on Mars.

speaker: narrator
en: Mikhail Anders. The man who made FSP. Twenty-eight years ago. A man who had been a miner. That was in both hands. The right hand cradled the left. The way he poured tea. That was this man's way.

speaker: narrator
en: Tea was poured. Two cups. One came forward. With both hands. It was received. Still hot. Hot things on Mars didn't last. It was right to receive. To receive now.

speaker: lena
en: Elder Mikhail, this one looks decent.

speaker: mikhail
en: Lena, don't scare them on their first day.

speaker: lena
en: I'm not scaring them! Just being honest.

speaker: narrator
en: Lena picked up her cup. One hand. Drank quickly. That was her way. Mikhail held his cup with both hands. Looked at it long. That was his way. Two ways in the same room.

speaker: mikhail
en: One rule. Nobody survives alone here. We help each other — or you leave.

speaker: mikhail
en: Amara recommended you. Her recommendation is enough for us.

speaker: mikhail
en: Rest today. Tomorrow is when it's real.

speaker: narrator
en: The village was walked. Night. The Martian night. Many stars. Because the atmosphere was thin. Clearer than Earth. Below that the village. Lights. Coming from windows. People were living.

speaker: narrator
en: A sound. A child's voice. Laughter. A child laughing on Mars. That was strangely surprising. Mars had become a place where children grew up. Seventeen years had made it so.

speaker: narrator
en: The names on the wall were looked at again. Chalk. Dates. Some names had a star mark beside them. What that was wasn't known. Whether they were names of the dead. Of those who had left. Or something else.

speaker: narrator
en: The mine was visible. Lights still on. Night shift. On Mars mines didn't stop. People took turns inside them. That was why this village existed.

speaker: yuna
en: You're new?

speaker: yuna
en: I'm Yuna. Born here. My father was a miner.

speaker: yuna
en: You were looking at the names on the wall, right? The star marks are people born here.

speaker: narrator
en: Yuna Kim. Twenty-one years old. Born on Mars. Mars 1.5 generation. What the first generation made and the next received. Children who had grown up. The newest and oldest things in this village.

speaker: yuna
en: You came for FSP?

speaker: yuna
en: Welcome. Elder Mikhail is a good person. Truly. It's hard to meet good people on Mars.

speaker: narrator
en: Dawn came. The Martian dawn. The sun rose slowly. Slower than Earth. The sky mixed red and yellow. First time seeing it. But not strange. There were moments when unfamiliar things felt natural. This was one.

speaker: narrator
en: Mikhail was outside at dawn. Alone. Holding tea. With both hands. Seen through a window. He was looking toward the mines. No words. That was this man's dawn.

speaker: narrator
en: Learned later. Mikhail's right leg. Mining accident. Old thing. It hurt more when the weather was bad. Bad weather days on Mars were many. But it was never seen mentioned. Nor stopping the tea making.

speaker: mikhail
en: Did you sleep?

speaker: mikhail
en: The first few days are hard because of gravity. Even though Mars is lighter than Earth the body's memory is different. A week and you'll be used to it.

speaker: mikhail
en: Today look at the village. Look at the people. That's the fastest way to understand FSP.

speaker: narrator
en: The village woke. People came out. Each had work. Those going to the mines. Those bringing out children. Those making food. Those repairing things. Everyone had rough hands. Everyone moved with familiarity.

speaker: narrator
en: Amara Okafor came. The person who had been unreachable. The reason for coming to Mars, half of it. She was waiting. Standing as if she had been waiting a long time and it was nothing.

speaker: amara
en: You came. Took a long time.

speaker: amara
en: How's Mars? First impression.

speaker: amara
en: You don't have to say. It's right not to know yet. Need a few more days to see.

speaker: narrator
en: Amara Okafor. FSP representative. From southern Hellas. A political person. But also an idealist. Both in one person. Whether that was possible on Mars wasn't known. Here it would be learned.

speaker: narrator
en: The mine was visible. The dawn shift started. People went inside. Someone waving. Someone nodding. Someone not looking back. Each their own way. The way of going inside.

speaker: narrator
en: Mikhail drank tea. Holding the cup with both hands. Looking at the mine. Finished it. Set the cup down. With the right hand. Looked at it a moment. The empty cup. Then began preparing the next cup.

speaker: narrator
en:
The tea was warm. For the first time.
This village felt like it could be home.
If home is possible on this planet.

The mine had lights. Names were on the wall. Children were laughing. Mikhail was pouring tea with both hands.

That was FSP.

speaker: narrator
en:
Time to Mars — 14 hours.
Black space beyond the cargo ship window.
You knew you wouldn't be coming back when this journey ended.

speaker: narrator
en: The ship was called Kariope. Full of cargo. Oxygen tanks. Food packs. Machine parts. And people. People loaded like cargo too. Not enough seats. Nobody complained. People who boarded this ship had already made their choice.

speaker: narrator
en:
2087. Mars population: 12 million.
Three factions divided this planet.
MCC — Mars Corporate Consortium. Those who hold the resources.
FSP — Free Settlers' Pact. Those who worked the land.
CV — Crimson Warlords. Those who live without law.

speaker: narrator
en: Mars was once a shared dream. Sixty years had passed. The shared dream divided into stakes. Stakes divided by negotiation. Negotiation ended with force. Now it was just like that. Like every place in the world eventually becomes.

speaker: narrator
en:
You received a summons from MCC.
The reason was simple — they needed someone like you.
What kind of person that was — you'd find out when you arrived on Mars.

speaker: narrator
en: Others were in the cargo bay. Miners. Tired faces. People too tired going to Mars. Or people going to Mars to become tired. Hard to tell the difference. On Mars it amounted to the same thing.

speaker: lifang
en: You're awake. Good.

speaker: lifang
en: I'm Lifang. MCC field director. Once you reach Mars, you're on my team.

speaker: lifang
en: Simple rules. Listen to me. Questions later.

speaker: lifang
en: Mars isn't Earth. Mistakes here mean death. People say that too lightly. I'm not saying it lightly.

speaker: narrator
en: Lifang looked out the window after speaking. Space was there. He said nothing more. That was his way. A person who said only what was necessary. People who had lived long on Mars became that way. People who knew words used oxygen.

speaker: lifang
en: MCC basic briefing. You may have heard this before. Listen anyway.

speaker: lifang
en: Hellas Central is base. MCC headquarters. Mineral refining. Administrative hub. Assignments come from there.

speaker: lifang
en: You can live on Mars without MCC. You can't live long. People who know that difference live longest.

speaker: narrator
en: There was an observation deck. A small window. People stood there. Looking out. Nothing. Just space. Still they looked. People trying to see Mars. It wasn't visible yet. Still they looked. That was the shape of hope. Looking for something not yet visible.

speaker: narrator
en: Twelve hours passed. Sleep came. Before sleeping looked out the window. A red dot was there. At first it looked like a star. As it grew closer — it became a planet. Blood-red. Beautiful. Frightening.

speaker: narrator
en: Two hours to landing. Announcement came. Masks on. Seatbelts. Entering Martian atmosphere. The voice was calm. A daily announcement. That calm felt strange. Strange that atmospheric entry could be daily and calm.

speaker: narrator
en: Mars filled the window. Red. Different from photos seen on Earth. Photos were flat. In reality it had depth. It looked alive. Mars wasn't alive. But it looked that way. That was Mars's first lie.

speaker: narrator
en: The docking bay. People disembarked. Miners. Engineers. Bureaucrats. Everyone wore masks. Masked faces were unreadable. No expressions. The first face of Mars. A mask.

speaker: lifang
en: We've arrived. Hellas Central docking station.

speaker: lifang
en: Masks always on. This zone is partial pressure. Indoors is fine but corridors and transit areas require masks.

speaker: lifang
en: First time so I'll say it. On Mars rules are broken for two reasons. Stupidity or long experience. I respect the second. The first has no place on my team.

speaker: narrator
